adelboden.intro: A valley head in the Bernese Oberland with waterfalls and a World Cup backdrop, a quiet half-day climb.

sides.character: From Frutigen steadily up the valley, a few hairpins before Adelboden.
sides.highlights: The Engstligen falls at the head of the valley.

alagna-valsesia.intro: The valley to the south-east side of Monte Rosa, a gentle day without a pass.

sides.character: From Varallo long and barely rising up the Sesia, only a little steeper past Riva Valdobbia.
sides.highlights: The Walser houses of Alagna and Monte Rosa at the head of the valley.

albulapass.intro: A quiet pass between the Albula valley and the Engadine, for long stretches beside the Rhaetian Railway's Albula line with its viaducts and spiral tunnels. Little traffic, plenty of landscape.

sides.character: From Filisur via Bergün and Preda in steps, with a tight rock passage at the Bergünerstein, then across an open plateau to the top.
sides.highlights: The Lai da Palpuogna above Preda.

sides.character: From La Punt short and steep at first in hairpins, flatter near the top. A short descent with views into the Engadine.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Upper Engadine.

alpe-d-huez.intro: The 21 numbered hairpins, each named after stage winners, make this the Tour's best-known climb. Fausto Coppi won the first summit finish here in 1952; today the fans party at Dutch Corner.

sides.character: From Bourg d'Oisans straight into steep hairpins, after which the gradient keeps changing. The signs count the hairpins down to the ski resort.
sides.highlights: Dutch Corner at hairpin 7 and the view back over the Oisans.

alpe-di-neggia.intro: From Lake Maggiore on the Gambarogno shore a good 1,000 metres of climbing in hairpins through chestnut forest, with the lake ever further below. Beyond the pass lies Indemini, a Swiss village connected to the road network only via Italy.

sides.character: From Vira on the lake in a long sequence of hairpins through chestnut forest, with flatter stretches between the steep ones. The lake at your back makes it the side to climb; downhill, the many tight bends are work.
sides.highlights: The view across Lake Maggiore towards Locarno.

sides.character: From Indemini short and evenly steep up to the pass. Downhill, the quick way over to Indemini and on into Italy.
sides.highlights: The stone village of Indemini.

altopiano-del-cansiglio.intro: The beech forest of the Cansiglio once supplied the Venetian Republic with timber for its fleet. Today the karst plateau is a quiet place of wide meadows and dense forest, above the plain and yet away from everything.

sides.character: From Vittorio Veneto long and in steps, with a marked descent on the way and some hairpins at the edge of the plateau. Dense beech forest at the top and almost no traffic.
sides.highlights: The open meadow basin of the Pian Cansiglio in the middle of the forest.

altopiano-di-asiago.intro: The plateau of the Seven Communes, wide and almost flat on top, with positions and memorials of the mountain war everywhere along its edges. The ascent is long; the real goal is the loops across the plateau.

sides.character: From Bassano long and flat to the foot of the plateau, then up its edge in steps and hairpins. A lot of distance for the height, nowhere steep for long.
sides.highlights: Above Asiago, the war memorial on the Leiten hill.

arcalis.intro: Andorra's summit finish, long and steady.

sides.character: From Ordino gently up the valley to El Serrat, then steadily in hairpins to the resort.
sides.highlights: The hairpins above El Serrat.

arlbergpass.intro: The Arlberg divides Tyrol from Vorarlberg and is the watershed between the Rhine and the Danube. At the top stands St. Christoph with its hospice, which dates back to the 14th century. Despite the tunnel the pass road remains a busy route.

sides.character: From Pians long and flat up the Stanzertal to St. Anton; it only gets steeper in the final part to the top. Few hairpins, more a long valley ride than a pass.
From Langen via Stuben short and steeper, uneven with a series of hairpins below the Arlberg peaks. Compact, and uphill the more entertaining side.

arolla.intro: The longest side valley of central Valais to its end: wooden villages, the Dent Blanche above the valley and at the top a climbers' village below the glaciers.

sides.character: In hairpins out of the Rhône valley to Vex, then long and moderate up the valley through Euseigne and Evolène; only the last kilometres from Les Haudères are steep, in hairpins.
sides.highlights: The earth pyramids of Euseigne, which the road passes through in a short tunnel, and the villages of Evolène and La Sage.

arosa.intro: A valley road with countless bends from Chur to the resort at the end of the Schanfigg. 1,100 m in one rhythm, with the Langwies viaduct halfway up.

sides.character: In hairpins up out of Chur and then long along the side of the Schanfigg, bend after bend with little change of gradient; steeper after Langwies up to Arosa.
sides.highlights: The Langwies viaduct of the Rhaetian Railway and at the top the Obersee in Arosa.

avoriaz.intro: The Tour climb above Morzine, easy to link with the Joux Plane and Les Gets.

sides.character: From Morzine steadily through forest and past avalanche galleries, higher up towards the rock edge of Avoriaz.
sides.highlights: The cliffs of Avoriaz and the view over the Morzine valley.

axalp.intro: A steep dead end above the turquoise Brienzersee, opposite the Brienzer Rothorn.

sides.character: From Brienz along the lakeshore and then steeply in hairpins through forest up to the alp.
sides.highlights: The view down onto the Brienzersee.

ballon-d-alsace.intro: In 1905 the first mountain the Tour de France ever climbed, and many times since. Wide roads from three sides; at the top pastures, inns and a statue of Joan of Arc where Alsace, Lorraine and Franche-Comté meet.

sides.character: From Saint-Maurice-sur-Moselle the shortest and steepest side, steadily around 7 % with hairpins through forest; a climb with a fixed rhythm.
From Giromagny long and gentle, with breathers on the way and wide bends; as a descent flowing and open.
From Sewen up the Doller valley at a changing gradient, easy and steeper stretches in turn, past a reservoir.
sides.highlights: The Lac d'Alfeld just above Sewen.

ballon-de-servance.intro: The crossing beside the Ballon de Servance is the first climb of Les 3 Ballons, which ride over it from Ronchamp to Le Thillot. A still forest road with moss and streams rather than a panorama; the summit itself lies off the road and is reached only on foot.

sides.character: From Plancher-les-Mines flat along the valley at first, then steady in the forest from the turn-off to the Planche des Belles Filles and clearly steeper over the last kilometres, with short double-digit ramps.
sides.highlights: The turn-off to the Planche des Belles Filles, which fits into the same ride.

sides.character: From Le Thillot over the Col des Croix, steady and never steep through the forest. As a descent narrow, bumpy and with loose grit in places – so better ridden up.
sides.highlights: The Col des Croix on the way, where the road passes from the Moselle side into Haute-Saône.

barrage-d-emosson.intro: A dead end on the French border that ends at a dam with a view of Mont Blanc. A Tour de France finish in 2016, reached over the Forclaz from Martigny or over the Montets from Chamonix.

sides.character: From Le Châtelard in hairpins up to Finhaut, then narrower and steeper along the rock face up to the dam.
sides.highlights: The crest of the dam with the view across the lake to Mont Blanc and the Aiguille Verte.

barrage-de-la-grande-dixence.intro: A dead end into the southern Valais Alps: from the town of Sion through villages and larch forest to the wall of the Grande Dixence dam, which closes the valley at the top.

sides.character: First in hairpins out of the Rhône valley to Vex, then long and even along the slope above the Val d'Hérémence; the last stretch narrow, in hairpins below the wall.
sides.highlights: The dam wall, which suddenly fills the whole valley, and the reservoir above it, a few minutes on foot.

berninapass.intro: The Bernina railway, a UNESCO World Heritage line, runs beside the road. From the north you look onto the Morteratsch glacier and Piz Palü; to the south the road drops steeply into the Italian-speaking Valposchiavo.

sides.character: Steadily and persistently steep from Poschiavo, through forest and then open via La Rösa, finally past Lago Bianco. The real climb.
sides.highlights: Lago Bianco just below the top.

sides.character: Gentle and stepped from Pontresina, almost without hairpins, with glaciers in view. Wide and flowing on the way down.
sides.highlights: The Morteratsch glacier and Piz Palü in view.

bielmonte.intro: A high road above the Biellese, the sister of the Oropa climb.

sides.character: From Trivero in waves and moderate along the ridge of the Panoramica Zegna, with short ramps.
sides.highlights: The rhododendrons and Monte Rosa to the north.

bocca-del-creer.intro: The high road over Monte Baldo: from Brentonico onto the ridge and over the Bocca di Navene down to Lake Garda, some 1,500 m above the water. The descent to the lake counts as the finest on the whole of Lake Garda.

sides.character: From Brentonico via San Valentino onto the ridge, with varying gradient through forest and alpine pasture. The shorter, controlled way up.
From the lake at Navene steep and narrow up the flank, then on along the ridge to the Bocca del Creer. Going down you ride with Lake Garda ahead of you, which makes it the side to descend.
sides.highlights: Lake Garda straight below the Bocca di Navene.

boedele.intro: A saddle between the Rhine valley and the Bregenzerwald, just behind Dornbirn. Vorarlberg's warm-up climb, with a long side and a short one.

sides.character: Steeply up out of the town via Watzenegg, then in hairpins through forest to the meadows at the saddle.
sides.highlights: The view across the Rhine valley to Lake Constance.

sides.character: From Schwarzenberg short and steep up across meadows, a fast, open descent into the Bregenzerwald.
sides.highlights: The village of Schwarzenberg with its wooden houses.

bosco-gurin.intro: The only German-speaking village in Ticino, at the end of a quiet mountain road.

sides.character: From Cevio in hairpins out of the Maggia valley, then steadily steep through forest and hamlets.
sides.highlights: The Walser houses of Bosco/Gurin.

brennerpass.intro: The busiest crossing of the Alps, but for cyclists it is the old main road away from the motorway. Not a mountain that asks much, rather the link between Innsbruck and South Tyrol that the Ötztaler rides between the Kühtai and the Jaufen.

sides.character: Out of Innsbruck first the steeper ramp up to Schönberg, then a long, almost level run up the Wipptal through Matrei and Steinach; just before the top it kicks up once more. You gain height without noticing, a rolling road in either direction.
sides.highlights: The Brennersee just below the top.

sides.character: From Sterzing flat out of town at first, the steeper stretch at Gossensass, then easy again up the upper Eisack valley. Shorter than the north side and with what little climbing the Brenner has.
sides.highlights: Gossensass at the mouth of the Pflersch valley.

breuil-cervinia.intro: The road to the Matterhorn from the south: a long Giro climb at whose end the pyramid stands above the ski resort.

sides.character: From Châtillon in hairpins out of the main valley, then long and even up the Valtournenche; more open from Valtournenche village.
sides.highlights: The Matterhorn, which appears at the top above the Lago Blu.

bruenigpass.intro: The low crossing between Obwalden and the Hasli valley, more link than destination.

sides.character: From Meiringen steadily along the slope with a view into the Hasli valley.
sides.highlights: The view to the Reichenbach falls and the Engelhörner.

sides.character: From Lungern short and steady above the Lungernsee.
sides.highlights: The Lungernsee below the road.

campo-carlo-magno.intro: Named after the legend that Charlemagne crossed the Alps here. Madonna di Campiglio made cycling history in 1999, when Marco Pantani, having won the Giro stage, was excluded the next morning over a high haematocrit reading.

sides.character: Up out of the Val Rendena in steps, with flatter sections and finally through the resort of Madonna di Campiglio. The side of the Giro finishes, and the more varied one to climb.
sides.highlights: The Brenta group comes right up to the road in the upper part.

sides.character: From the Val di Sole at Dimaro through forest and a handful of hairpins, steepest low down and easing towards the top. An even road, good to ride in either direction.

capanna-dotra.intro: A narrow spur off the Lukmanier's south side up to the Capanna Dötra on an alp above the Blenio valley. Hardly any traffic and a quiet detour.

sides.character: Steep and narrow straight from the junction, easing towards the top onto the alp.

cari.intro: A hairpin road out of the Leventina up to a small ski village, an insider's tip next to the Gotthard.

sides.character: From Faido straight into hairpins up the slope, steadily steep through chestnut and larch forest.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Leventina.

ceillac-vallee-du-melezet.intro: A quiet dead end from the Guil valley up to Ceillac and on into the Vallée du Mélézet. A peaceful counterpoint to the big passes of the Queyras.

sides.character: From the Maison du Roy straight into steep hairpins out of the valley, then flatter steps to Ceillac and a final rise into the valley head.
sides.highlights: The village of Ceillac in its wide basin.

chaillol.intro: A quiet resort climb above the Champsaur, a good companion to the Col du Noyer.

sides.character: From Saint-Bonnet through the Champsaur villages steadily to the resort.
sides.highlights: The view of the Vieux Chaillol and the Obiou.

chamrousse.intro: The long forest climb above Grenoble into the Belledonne.

sides.character: From Uriage steadily at 7 to 8 % through dense forest, hardly any views until the top.
sides.highlights: At the top the view over Grenoble and the Vercors.

chasseral.intro: The highest pass of the Bernese Jura, with the view of the three lakes.

sides.character: From Saint-Imier steadily through forest, across open pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The Chasseral pastures.

sides.character: From Nods steeper up the south flank with a view of Lake Biel.
sides.highlights: Lake Biel and the Alpine chain.

cima-grappa.intro: A lone mountain above the Venetian plain, with more than 1,500 m of climbing in one go from every side. In the 2014 Giro d'Italia an uphill time trial finished here, won by Nairo Quintana; at the top the First World War ossuary and the view to the Adriatic.

sides.character: From Semonzo narrow and irregular through a long series of hairpins, shadeless in the upper part. The rougher, steeper ascent, more impressive uphill than down.
From Possagno long and in steps, with a short descent on the way and a few steep ramps in between. Varied, but without a clear preferred direction.
sides.highlights: At the start in Possagno, the temple of the sculptor Antonio Canova.

sides.character: From Romano d'Ezzelino the wider main road, long even hairpins and steeper towards the top. Easy to read, and the most pleasant of the three sides to descend.
sides.highlights: With every hairpin the view across the plain towards the lagoon widens.

cinque-torri.intro: A steep spur up to the five rock towers above Cortina, where Italian artillery stood in the First World War. Today the area is an open-air museum with restored positions.

sides.character: From the junction on the Falzarego road straight away at around 10 % and barely easing, with few hairpins, first through forest, then open below the towers.
sides.highlights: The five towers up close and views of the Tofana and the Croda da Lago

cipressa.intro: Since 1982 the penultimate climb of Milan–Sanremo and often the place where the race breaks apart. A short hill through olive groves to the village above the coast, famous but not hard.

sides.character: Up from the Aurelia at San Lorenzo, with varying gradient and a few hairpins among the olives; hard at race pace, a quarter of an hour at your own.
sides.highlights: The village of Cipressa at the top with a view of the sea.

cirque-du-fer-a-cheval.intro: A valley head near Sixt, ringed by a semicircle of 700-metre walls with waterfalls pouring down them. Six easy kilometres to one of the great sights of the Northern Alps.

sides.character: From Sixt-Fer-à-Cheval almost flat along the Giffre, a few gentle steps and hardly a bend. The walls draw closer with every kilometre.
sides.highlights: The waterfalls in the semicircle of the valley head.

cogne.intro: The gateway to the Gran Paradiso: a gorge road that opens out at the top into a wide basin of meadows.

sides.character: From the vineyards of Aymavilles into the gorge and then long and steady along the Grand Eyvia, with no steep sections.
sides.highlights: The meadows of Sant'Orso in front of the village and the view into the Valnontey to the Gran Paradiso.

col-d-agnes.intro: The most beautiful pass in the Ariège, across endless pastures.

sides.character: From Aulus steeply through forest, across the pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The pastures below the pass.

sides.character: From Massat long via Le Port and the Port de Lers.
sides.highlights: The Étang de Lers.

col-d-allos.intro: With the Cayolle and the Champs the Allos forms the triple loop from Barcelonnette. The north side is a narrow balcony road high above the Bachelard gorge, the south side climbs more calmly up the upper Verdon valley.

sides.character: Narrow and stepped from Barcelonnette along the flank above the gorge, often without a guard rail, then open pastures at the top. A joy uphill, delicate downhill.
Long and gentle from Colmars up the Verdon valley via Allos and La Foux, on a wider road. The better descent.
sides.highlights: The fortified old town of Colmars at the start.

col-d-aspin.intro: The most beautiful of the classic Pyrenean passes, steady and with an open view.

sides.character: From Arreau steadily through forest, across open pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The pastures with animals on the road.

sides.character: From Sainte-Marie via Payolle gently, briefly steeper at the top.
sides.highlights: The Lac de Payolle.

col-d-aubisque.intro: The classic of the Béarn, crowned by the cliff road to the Soulor.

sides.character: From Laruns via Eaux-Bonnes, then steep and irregular with ramps around 10 % to Gourette and across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The view from the pass to the Pic de Ger.

sides.character: From Argelès via Arrens to the Soulor, then rolling on the road cut into the cliff of the Cirque du Litor.
sides.highlights: The corniche of the Cirque du Litor.

col-d-azet.intro: The link from Saint-Lary towards Luchon, across pastures with a view of the peaks.

sides.character: From Saint-Lary via Azet steadily steep across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The view of the border peaks.

sides.character: From Génos short and steep in hairpins.
sides.highlights: The Génos-Loudenvielle lake.

col-d-ey.intro: The home climb of Buis-les-Baronnies and the opener of almost every loop there. Short and friendly between olive groves and apricot orchards, with a view of the Ventoux at the top.

sides.character: From Buis up between olives and apricots, gentle below, a little steeper at the top with a few hairpins; the classic way into the loop.
sides.highlights: The view of the Ventoux from the top.

sides.character: From Sainte-Jalle short and almost straight, steeper towards the top; as a descent northwards a short, open stretch.

col-d-eze.intro: For decades the closing act of Paris–Nice, as a mountain time trial up from Nice. The Grande Corniche leads to the col with the sea below, and La Turbie and Monaco lie beyond.

sides.character: Out of Nice onto the Grande Corniche, uneven with steeper ramps and easier stretches, hardly any hairpins; the sea below you all the way, and plenty of traffic.
sides.highlights: The view over the Baie des Anges and Nice from the Corniche.

col-d-ispeguy.intro: A short, green border pass for a loop from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port.

sides.character: From Baïgorry steadily in hairpins across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The Baïgorry valley.

sides.character: From Errazu gently through forest.
sides.highlights: The Baztan valley.

col-d-izoard.intro: The scree desert of the Casse Déserte makes the Izoard unmistakable; a memorial there honours Fausto Coppi and Louison Bobet. A Tour classic between Briançon and the Queyras.

sides.character: From Briançon via Cervières with flatter stretches, then many hairpins through larch forest to the top. Good climbing, a twisty descent.
sides.highlights: The memorial at the top with the view back to the Écrins.

sides.character: From Guillestre long and flat at first through the Guil gorge, steeper from Arvieux, finally through the Casse Déserte. The classic climb, with its highlight at the end.
sides.highlights: The Casse Déserte with the Coppi–Bobet memorial.

col-d-oderen.intro: A gentle, wooded crossing from the upper Thur valley to Ventron in the Moselotte valley. No highlight on its own, but a quiet link between Alsace and Lorraine.

sides.character: From Fellering the longer side, moderate and stepped with easier stretches through forest; as a descent long and unproblematic.
From Ventron short, a little steeper towards the top, through forest; a compact climb.

col-d-ornon.intro: The Ornon is the friendly pass of the Oisans: even, open all year and away from the bustle around Alpe d'Huez. It links Le Bourg-d'Oisans with the quiet Valbonnais.

sides.character: From Le Bourg-d'Oisans through the narrow gorge of the Lignarre, then up the valley in gentle steps. Few hairpins, more a long roll uphill.
sides.highlights: On the way the hairpin road to Villard-Reymond branches off.

col-de-bagargui.intro: The finest pass in the French Basque country.

sides.character: From Larrau steeply in hairpins across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The view of the Pic d'Orhy.

sides.character: From Mendive long and moderate via the Iraty chalets.
sides.highlights: The Iraty beech forest.

col-de-bleine.intro: The highest crossing between the Estéron and the Thorenc plateau. Beech forest and hairpins lower down, meadows and limestone ridges at the top, high above the Riviera.

sides.character: From Saint-Auban in hairpins through beech forest, stepped with easier stretches and a short dip on the way; meadows and limestone at the top.
sides.highlights: The beech forest in the hairpins of the north side.

sides.character: From the Thorenc plateau only a gentle, rolling rise without hairpins; the better descent, open and quiet.
sides.highlights: A wide view over meadows and limestone ridges at the top.

col-de-bramont.intro: A quiet crossing from La Bresse into the uppermost Thur valley at Wildenstein, short and steady. No big name, but a pleasant building block for loops between the Thur and the Moselotte.

sides.character: From Wildenstein steadily up through forest in a run of hairpins; you see them coming and ride them in rhythm.
sides.highlights: The Kruth-Wildenstein reservoir at the foot.

sides.character: From La Bresse gentle and only a little steeper at the top, hardly any hairpins; as a descent the more flowing side.

col-de-braus.intro: In the hinterland of Nice, where the pros train in winter, the Braus is a fixture. It is known for the ladder of hairpins above L'Escarène, laid into the slope like a drawing.

sides.character: From L'Escarène straight into the ladder of hairpins, with the steepest bits early and easier going towards the top. One hairpin follows the next, and the view keeps falling back into the valley.
sides.highlights: From above the view of the hairpin ladder over L'Escarène.

col-de-brouis.intro: The crossing from Sospel into the Roya valley at Breil, linking Sospel with Tende and the railway line. An honest mid-height pass between olive slopes and forest, easy to combine with the Castillon and the Braus.

sides.character: From Sospel in many hairpins with a changing gradient, easier and steeper stretches in turn; as a descent twisty but not steep.
From Breil steadily and noticeably steeper out of the Roya valley, with more climbing over a shorter distance; the side to climb.
sides.highlights: Breil-sur-Roya on the river, with the view back into the Roya valley.

col-de-bussang.intro: The N66 between Thann and Remiremont, flat enough to link rides and with heavy traffic and lorries. Not a goal, just a passage; the Moselle rises at the top.

sides.character: From Saint-Maurice-sur-Moselle flat and straight on the main road, without hairpins; quickly done, but with lorries beside you.
sides.highlights: The source of the Moselle at the top.

sides.character: From Urbès steadily in a few hairpins, more height than from the west; here too on the busy main road.

col-de-castillon.intro: The direct way from Menton on the sea to Sospel in the Bévéra valley. Through the Careï gorge and past the rebuilt village of Castillon, a pass that takes you from the beach into the mountains in a few kilometres.

sides.character: From Menton at sea level through the Careï gorge, in steps with many hairpins; the lower part has traffic, it gets quieter higher up.
sides.highlights: The village of Castillon just below the top, with a view back to the sea.

sides.character: From Sospel short and steady, with a few hairpins; in this direction a manageable descent into the Bévéra valley.
sides.highlights: Sospel with its old bridge over the Bévéra.

col-de-champex.intro: A small pass road up to Champex-Lac, the resort on a mountain lake below the Grand Combin massif. It runs parallel to the lower part of the Great St Bernard road and is the quiet detour between Martigny and Orsières.

sides.character: From Les Valettes first through a gorge, then in many tight hairpins through forest, steepest at the bottom and easing towards the top; narrow and little used.
sides.highlights: The lake of Champex-Lac, where the road arrives at the top.

sides.character: From Orsières steadily in hairpins over meadows and through forest, a wider road with the PostBus line; flowing as a descent.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Val d'Entremont and onto Orsières.

col-de-chateauneuf.intro: The first mountain behind Nice towards Tourrette-Levens and Contes, and the opener of many training loops out of the city. Not lonely, but reached within an hour from the sea.

sides.character: From Saint-André-de-la-Roche long and stepped up from the edge of the city, almost without hairpins and with traffic; as a descent wide and quick back to Nice.
From Contes up the slope in a dense run of hairpins, stepped with one steeper pitch; the side to climb.

col-de-fontaube.intro: From Buis via Eygaliers onto a ridge and down into the Toulourenc valley, right beneath the north face of the Ventoux. A small pass with almost no traffic, linking the Baronnies with Brantes and Montbrun.

sides.character: From Eygaliers moderately up in a few hairpins, with easier sections; the real climb of the pass.
From the Toulourenc valley at Brantes hardly a climb; in the other direction the descent with the north face of the Ventoux ahead.
sides.highlights: The north face of the Ventoux above the Toulourenc valley.

col-de-grosse-pierre.intro: A short wooded crossing between Gérardmer and the Moselotte valley at Cornimont. Unassuming, but with a steep pitch on the north side that is not to be underestimated.

sides.character: From Gérardmer short and stepped, without hairpins, with one steep ramp between easier stretches and a short dip; the more interesting side to climb.
From Cornimont longer and gentler through forest, with short ramps; the calmer side to descend.

col-de-jau.intro: A lonely pass on the eastern edge of the Pyrenees, with the Canigou at your back.

sides.character: From Mosset steadily through forest and across pastures.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Canigou.

sides.character: From Axat long through the Aude valley and forest.
sides.highlights: The Aude gorges.

col-de-joux.intro: A crossing between the Aosta valley and the Val d'Ayas: a long hairpin ramp on one side, a short stretch on the other.

sides.character: From Saint-Vincent steadily steep in many hairpins through forest and hamlets, more than 1,000 m without a flat section.
sides.highlights: The view back across the Aosta valley and the larch meadows at the pass.

sides.character: From Brusson only a short, moderate climb through larch forest; as a descent the link into the Val d'Ayas.
sides.highlights: The view up the Val d'Ayas to the Monte Rosa.

col-de-joux-plane.intro: The classic last climb before the descent to Morzine in the Tour de France; in 2000 Lance Armstrong suffered his famous bonk here. At the top a small lake and a view of Mont Blanc.

sides.character: Steadily steep from Samoëns with no real let-up: first through forest and hairpins, then over open pastures at the top. Not a place for a bad day.
sides.highlights: Mont Blanc appears over the last kilometres.

col-de-l-echelle.intro: The shortcut from the Clarée to Bardonecchia, larches and pastures at the top.

sides.character: From Plampinet short and moderate through larches to the plateau.
sides.highlights: The larch forests of the upper Clarée.

sides.character: From Bardonecchia via Melezet, then steeply in tight hairpins up the rock step, with short tunnels.
sides.highlights: The hairpins on the rock step above Melezet.

col-de-l-homme-mort.intro: The crossing from Montbrun-les-Bains onto the lavender plateau of Ferrassières and Sault. From the west it is hardly a climb, but from Montbrun it is a quiet forest road with a view of the Montagne de Lure.

sides.character: From Montbrun long and mostly moderate through forest, with easier stretches and one short steeper pitch; the plateau opens out at the top.
sides.highlights: The view of the Montagne de Lure, and at the top the lavender fields of the plateau.

col-de-l-iseran.intro: The highest road pass in the Alps links the Haute Maurienne with the Isère valley. In 2019 a Tour stage was stopped after the crossing because of hail and a mudslide.

sides.character: From Bonneval up a lonely, treeless high valley, with a changing gradient and hard pitches in the upper part. Wild and remote, the finer side to climb.
sides.highlights: The view back to Bonneval and the glaciers of the Haute Maurienne.

sides.character: From Val d'Isère gentle at first, then in hairpins through the ski area, steeper near the top. Wider and more even; a readable descent with Val d'Isère ahead.

col-de-l-orme.intro: Really only the first step from Lucéram up to Peïra-Cava and the Col de Turini. Hardly worth mentioning as a pass, but the road on which the loops from Nice over the Turini begin.

sides.character: From Lucéram steadily up the slope in many hairpins, a short, solid climb that carries straight on towards Peïra-Cava.
sides.highlights: The view back down to Lucéram from the hairpins.

col-de-la-bataille.intro: A Vercors pass whose top lies just past a short tunnel through the rock, after which the view opens over the Combe de Bouvante. With the Combe Laval and the Col de la Machine it makes one of the finest loops in the Vercors.

sides.character: From Léoncel through forest, with a long stretch just under 9 % in the first half, the last two kilometres almost flat. The tunnel just before the col is windy.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Combe de Bouvante after the tunnel.

col-de-la-biche.intro: The Colombier's neighbour, easy to link in a loop along the ridge.

sides.character: From Champagne steadily through forest, narrow at the top.
sides.highlights: The forests of the Valromey.

sides.character: From Hotonnes gently across the plateau and through forest.
sides.highlights: The pastures of the Hotonnes plateau.

col-de-la-bonette.intro: The loop around the Cime de la Bonette is the highest paved road in France, and the Tour has crossed it several times. Two very long, lonely sides with military ruins from the old border defences.

sides.character: From Jausiers long and even through larches, then in many hairpins over the bare slopes at Restefond. A steady rhythm that suits the climb.
sides.highlights: The barracks at Restefond and finally the loop around the Cime.

sides.character: From Saint-Étienne-de-Tinée even longer, but even and with fewer hairpins, up a lonely valley with wide bends. A long, open descent.
sides.highlights: The ruins of the Camp des Fourches.

col-de-la-cayolle.intro: The Cayolle links Barcelonnette with the upper Var valley and is part of the Route des Grandes Alpes. Narrow and hardly used, through the Bachelard gorge in the north and past the source of the Var in the south.

sides.character: From Barcelonnette first squeezed through the Bachelard gorge, then in steps up an open high valley with flatter stretches. Gentle, long and lonely.
sides.highlights: The narrow Bachelard gorge in the lower part.

sides.character: Long and stepped from Guillaumes through the villages of the upper Var valley, never steep. Hardly any traffic either way.
sides.highlights: The Var rises near Estenc.

col-de-la-colombiere.intro: A Tour classic between the Arve valley and the Aravis, right below the limestone walls of the Bargy range. The two sides differ: steepening from Scionzier, even from Le Grand-Bornand.

sides.character: From Scionzier moderate for a long time to Le Reposoir, then it steepens and the last kilometres climb below the rock walls. A climb that builds.
sides.highlights: The charterhouse of Le Reposoir on the way.

sides.character: Even from Le Grand-Bornand over alpine meadows and in hairpins, with open views. The more flowing side downhill.

col-de-la-core.intro: A steady pass in the Couserans with a view of the Mont Valier.

sides.character: From Seix steadily through forest and across pastures.
sides.highlights: The Mont Valier.

sides.character: From Castillon through the Bethmale valley past the lake.
sides.highlights: The Lac de Bethmale.

col-de-la-couillole.intro: A quiet crossing between the Tinée valley and Valberg that starts from very low down. Paris–Nice has finished at the top more than once; Tadej Pogačar won there in 2023.

sides.character: Long and even from Saint-Sauveur-sur-Tinée, in hairpins up bare slopes and past the perched village of Roubion. The real climb, narrow for a descent.
sides.highlights: The perched village of Roubion halfway up.

sides.character: Only a short step from Beuil, with a small dip on the way, over open upland. The easy way down.

col-de-la-croix.intro: Narrow, steep and quiet: the mountain road from Villars to Les Diablerets that leaves the valley road behind and crosses the alpine pastures. At the top the view of the Grand Muveran.

sides.character: Up from Villars in steps, steep pitches alternating with short flatter ones, almost without hairpins. The higher you go, the more open the pastures.
sides.highlights: The pastures at the top with the view of the Muveran.

col-de-la-croix-de-fer.intro: Named after the iron cross at the top and often ridden together with the nearby Glandon. A long, restless pass with counter-climbs between the Maurienne and the Oisans.

sides.character: From Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne long and stepped, with flat stretches and counter-climbs, then via Saint-Sorlin-d'Arves through open pasture.
sides.highlights: The Aiguilles d'Arves above Saint-Sorlin.

sides.character: From the Oisans via Allemont, with a long intermediate descent that gives away much height, then past the Lac de Grand Maison. Up and down in either direction.
sides.highlights: The Grand Maison reservoir below the top.

col-de-la-croix-de-la-serra.intro: A moderate pass in the Haut-Jura, quiet and through forest.

sides.character: From Saint-Claude up the Tacon valley and across pastures, steadily.
sides.highlights: The pastures and forests of the Haut-Jura.

col-de-la-croix-fry.intro: The quiet pass between Thônes and La Clusaz, a good pairing with the Aravis and the Colombière.

sides.character: From Thônes gently into the Manigod valley at first, then steadier and steeper across pastures and chalets to the top.
sides.highlights: The hamlets of Manigod and at the top the limestone walls of the Aravis.

sides.character: From La Clusaz short and steady through forest and ski slopes.
sides.highlights: The view back to La Clusaz and the Aravis.

col-de-la-faucille.intro: The home climb of Geneva's cyclists, with Lake Geneva as the backdrop.

sides.character: From Gex steadily in long hairpins through forest.
sides.highlights: Lake Geneva and Mont Blanc.

sides.character: From Mijoux short through the Valserine valley.
sides.highlights: The Valserine valley.

col-de-la-forclaz-de-montmin.intro: The pass above the Lac d'Annecy where paragliders launch on fine days. From the top the whole lake lies beneath you, which is why, despite its short ascent, it is one of the classics around Annecy.

sides.character: From Talloires moderately at first above the lakeshore, then increasingly steep towards the top, with the last kilometres the hardest. The lake stays behind you almost all the way.
sides.highlights: At the top the view straight down onto the Lac d'Annecy and the launching paragliders.

col-de-la-forclaz-martigny.intro: The crossing from Martigny into the Trient valley and on to Chamonix, one of the main roads between the Valais and the Mont Blanc area. The Tour de France crossed it in 2016 on the way to Finhaut-Emosson.

sides.character: Out of the Rhône valley in many hairpins through the vineyards, then through forest, steeper if anything towards the top. Steady, hard work with a growing view back over the valley.
sides.highlights: The view back to Martigny and the bend of the Rhône.

col-de-la-givrine.intro: From Lake Geneva onto the Jura, more than 800 m in one go.

sides.character: From Nyon gently through the vineyards, then steadily in hairpins through forest to Saint-Cergue and the top.
sides.highlights: The view back over Lake Geneva.

col-de-la-lebe.intro: An easy Bugey pass, as an approach to the Colombier or as a quiet day.

sides.character: From Champagne gently through forest.
sides.highlights: The Valromey.

sides.character: From Belley long and gentle through the villages of the Bugey.
sides.highlights: The vineyards of the Bugey.

col-de-la-lombarde.intro: From Isola the road climbs through the ski station of Isola 2000 to the Italian border, then winds down in many hairpins into the Stura valley to Vinadio. The Giro crossed it in 2016, finishing at Sant'Anna di Vinadio.

sides.character: Long and irregular out of the Tinée valley, with many hairpins up to Isola 2000 and above it on a wider road. The better descent of the two.
The Italian side is narrower: irregularly steep in many hairpins through forest and pastures, passing the turn-off to Sant'Anna near the top.
sides.highlights: The detour to the Santuario di Sant'Anna.

col-de-la-loze.intro: Only on the Tour since 2020, and a legend at once: the upper part is a narrow, car-free cycle road with constantly changing ramps. In 2023 Tadej Pogačar cracked here, and Jonas Vingegaard turned his yellow jersey into a decisive lead.

sides.character: From Brides-les-Bains on the road to Méribel, then on the cycle road with short steep ramps and flat bits to the top. Made for climbing.
sides.highlights: The car-free cycle road above the treeline.

sides.character: From Courchevel shorter and calmer, through the ski area in hairpins to the top. The easier choice for the descent.

col-de-la-madeleine.intro: A regular on the Tour since 1969, with two very long sides between the Maurienne and the Tarentaise. A pass for endurance, hardly spectacular but honestly hard.

sides.character: From La Chambre almost constantly around 8 %, many hairpins through forest and pasture, with no let-up. The steady rhythm rewards the climb.
sides.highlights: At the top a view as far as Mont Blanc.

sides.character: From the Isère side uneven: steep pitches, flat stretches and a short dip. As a descent it is varied, with breathers in between.

col-de-la-madeleine-bedoin.intro: A small saddle between Malaucène and Bédoin that closes the loop round Mont Ventoux. Hardly a climb, but with an open view of the Ventoux and the jagged Dentelles de Montmirail; it shares only its name with the great Madeleine in Savoie.

sides.character: From Malaucène gently through vineyards and pines, with short flat stretches; a warm-up rather than an effort.
sides.highlights: The Ventoux on your left, the Dentelles de Montmirail to the west.

sides.character: From Bédoin flat and slightly rolling, without hairpins; in either direction a link you ride almost without changing gear.
sides.highlights: Bédoin, the Ventoux start town with its cafés, at the foot.

col-de-la-madone.intro: From sea level in Menton to over 900 m: the Madone is the form test of the pros on the Côte d'Azur, where times were compared for years. With only a village at the top, it is almost free of traffic.

sides.character: From Menton moderate at first, then getting steeper towards the top past the perched village of Sainte-Agnès. Many hairpins over dry slopes, the sea always below.
sides.highlights: Near Sainte-Agnès the view down onto Menton and the sea.

col-de-la-pierre-saint-martin.intro: A long, hard border pass with a limestone desert at the top.

sides.character: From Arette long through the Barétous, steep at the top to the resort and across the karst.
sides.highlights: The karst fields on the border.

sides.character: From Isaba long and moderate through the Roncal valley and forest.
sides.highlights: The Belagua valley.

col-de-la-porte.intro: A quiet crossing above Coaraze over to Lucéram, a little higher than the neighbouring Col Saint-Roch. Hardly any traffic, and on the way the view over the villages of the Paillon valleys.

sides.character: From Coaraze long and stepped, with hairpins, easier stretches and a dip on the way; you gain more height than the average suggests.
sides.highlights: The view over the villages of the Paillon.

col-de-la-ramaz.intro: A Chablais pass for those seeking quiet: hardly any traffic, a steep middle section around 10 % and a gallery. At the top no ski resort, just alpine pasture.

sides.character: From Taninges in steps: after a moderate start comes the steep middle section with the gallery, then it eases again up to the pasture.

col-de-la-schlucht.intro: The main crossing from Colmar to Gérardmer, and on the Tour de France route in 2023. The Route des Crêtes starts at the top; the traffic, though, comes with it.

sides.character: From Munster long and steady up the valley, with hairpins and rock above the road near the top; the finer and steeper side.
sides.highlights: The view back into the Munster valley from the upper hairpins.

sides.character: From Gérardmer via Xonrupt almost flat, with short steps; more a roll over than a climb, so the side for the descent.
sides.highlights: The lake at Gérardmer at the foot.

col-de-latrape.intro: The gentle approach to the Agnes.

sides.character: From Ercé long and gentle up the valley, briefly steeper at the top.
sides.highlights: The Garbet valley.

col-de-macuegne.intro: A quiet pass between Montbrun-les-Bains and Séderon, over lavender fields and through beech forest. On the Perty loop it is the way back, with the Ventoux in view.

sides.character: From Montbrun steadily over lavender fields into the beech forest, with the Ventoux at your back; in the other direction a calm descent towards the mountain.
sides.highlights: Montbrun-les-Bains, built against the slope, with the Ventoux behind it.

sides.character: From Séderon shorter, a little steeper towards the top, with a few hairpins through forest; the direction of the Perty loop.

col-de-manse.intro: The short crossing from Gap into the Champsaur, the opener for the Noyer and Chaillol.

sides.character: From Gap steadily across meadows and forest up to the plateau.
sides.highlights: The view over the Gap basin.

sides.character: From Saint-Laurent-du-Cros short and gentle.
sides.highlights: The Champsaur with the Vieux Chaillol.

col-de-marie-blanque.intro: Low but mean: the short Tour pass with the steep finale.

sides.character: From Escot moderate through forest at first, then four kilometres at around 11 % to the top.
sides.highlights: The forest above the Vallée d'Aspe.

sides.character: From Bielle gently across the Bénou plateau.
sides.highlights: The Bénou plateau with its herds.

col-de-menee.intro: A long, gentle pass without traffic, with the Mont Aiguille as its landmark.

sides.character: From Châtillon long and gentle through the Bès valley and forest up to the tunnel.
sides.highlights: The gorges of the Diois.

sides.character: From Chichilianne steadily across pastures and forest.
sides.highlights: The Mont Aiguille right above the road.

col-de-mente.intro: Short, steep and part of the chain to the Portet d'Aspet.

sides.character: From Saint-Béat steeply in hairpins via Boutx.
sides.highlights: The view of the Garonne.

sides.character: From Juzet long and moderate through forest via the Ger.
sides.highlights: The Comminges forests.

col-de-montgenevre.intro: One of the oldest crossings of the Alps; the Romans already passed here on their way to Italy. Today it is the main road from Briançon to Turin, open all year, for cyclists more a link than a destination.

sides.character: From Briançon on a wide, well-built road in moderate steps, a few broad hairpins and plenty of traffic. Behind you the fortifications of Briançon fall away.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Vauban fortifications of Briançon.

col-de-murs.intro: Over the Monts de Vaucluse from the Ventoux country into the Luberon: limestone, oaks and lavender, with hardly any traffic. The village of Murs lies on the way, and beyond it the road drops to Gordes.

sides.character: From Venasque gently at first, then gradually steeper through oak woods and limestone, with a few hairpins higher up; the longer and finer ascent.
sides.highlights: Venasque, one of the villages above the Comtat, at the start.

sides.character: From the village of Murs only a short, moderate rise; as a descent the quiet side towards Gordes and the Luberon.

col-de-nice.intro: A short hill between the two Paillon valleys of L'Escarène and Contes. Not a goal on its own, but with the Braus and the Saint-Roch a link in the loops behind Nice.

sides.character: From L'Escarène only a short, steady stretch with two hairpins; done in a few minutes.

col-de-notre-dame-des-abeilles.intro: The forest road over the southern flank of the Ventoux from Bédoin to Sault, even and without big hairpin sequences. Besides the Gorges de la Nesque the second way onto the lavender plateau of Sault, quieter and more wooded.

sides.character: From Flassan at an even gradient through oak and pine forest, with a few easier sections; the real climb of the two, a calm ride.
From Sault across the plateau more a rolling rise with a short dip than a climb; in this direction you earn the long, even descent to Flassan.
sides.highlights: Lavender fields around Sault behind you.

col-de-pailheres.intro: The big pass of the eastern Pyrenees, over 2,000 m and almost traffic-free.

sides.character: From Ax via Ascou, then steep through forest and in tight hairpins across the pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The hairpins below the top.

sides.character: From Usson through the Donezan, shorter and steadily steep.
sides.highlights: The quiet Donezan.

col-de-perty.intro: One of the highest passes in the Baronnies, ridden by the Tour de France in 2006. From the forest of the Ouvèze the road climbs into a wide bowl, with the Ventoux and the Montagne de Lure on the horizon at the top.

sides.character: From Saint-Auban long and leisurely, with hairpins and easier stretches, out of the forest into the open bowl; as a descent wide and flowing.
sides.highlights: The open bowl below the summit with the view to the Ventoux.

sides.character: From Laborel shorter and steeper, increasingly so towards the top, with a few hairpins; the side that suits climbing.

col-de-peyresourde.intro: Luchon's gateway to the west, continued by the Aspin and the Tourmalet.

sides.character: From Luchon via Saint-Aventin at a steady 7 %, across open slopes at the top.
sides.highlights: The view back into the Luchon valley.

sides.character: From Arreau long and gentle through the Louron valley, steeper in hairpins at the top.
sides.highlights: The Loudenvielle lake.

col-de-plainpalais.intro: The gateway from Chambéry into the Bauges nature park.

sides.character: From Saint-Alban-Leysse steadily through the Leysse gorge and forest to Les Déserts and the top.
sides.highlights: The view back over Chambéry.

sides.character: From Le Châtelard long and gentle through the Chéran valley and across pastures.
sides.highlights: The quiet villages of the Bauges.

col-de-port.intro: The easy pass between the Ariège valley and the Couserans.

sides.character: From Tarascon long and gentle through forest.
sides.highlights: The Ariège forests.

sides.character: From Massat steadily through forest and meadows.
sides.highlights: The Massat valley.

col-de-puymorens.intro: The crossing into the Cerdagne, wide high pastures at the top.

sides.character: From L'Hospitalet steadily in hairpins across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The high pastures of the upper Ariège.

sides.character: From Porté short and gentle.
sides.highlights: The Cerdagne.

col-de-richemond.intro: The gentle pass at the northern end of the Colombier massif.

sides.character: From Corbonod long and moderate in hairpins above the Rhône valley and through forest.
sides.highlights: The view across the Rhône valley at Seyssel.

sides.character: From Hotonnes short and gentle.
sides.highlights: The Hotonnes plateau.

col-de-romme.intro: Since 2009 the Romme has been known as the hard starter before the Colombière when the Tour rides the two back to back. It clings like a balcony above the Arve valley and saves its steepest part for the top.

sides.character: From Cluses gently for a long time, then in steps much steeper on a narrow road above the valley. The average deceives: the upper part is far harder than the lower.
sides.highlights: Views straight down into the Arve valley from the balcony road.

col-de-saint-jean.intro: A short, quiet crossing in the Baronnies between the Céans valley at Laborel and the Méouge valley at Eygalayes. At the top stand a small chapel and a viewpoint; together with the Perty and the Macuègne it makes a loop almost without traffic.

sides.character: From Laborel short and steady between lavender and forest, with a few hairpins; quickly at the top.
sides.highlights: Lavender fields on the lower slope above Laborel.

sides.character: From Eygalayes longer, steeper above the village and with a few hairpins near the top; the surface is rough in places.
sides.highlights: The chapel at the summit.

col-de-sainte-marie.intro: The old crossing from Sainte-Marie-aux-Mines into Lorraine. Since most through traffic now takes the Maurice-Lemaire tunnel below it, the pass road has become much quieter.

sides.character: From Sainte-Marie-aux-Mines steeper and steeper towards the top, hardly any hairpins, through forest; the longer climb with the stronger finish.
From Wisembach short and noticeably steep, more so towards the top; a compact climb without hairpins.

col-de-sarenne.intro: The Sarenne is the back door of Alpe d'Huez: in the 2013 Tour the race descended it between its two ascents to L'Alpe, much debated at the time for the poor surface. Otherwise hardly anyone comes up here.

sides.character: Short and punchy from Clavans-en-Haut: tight hairpins across open alpine slopes, getting steeper towards the top. No trees, no houses, just the road on the hillside.
sides.highlights: Over the top on into the ski area and down to Alpe d'Huez.

col-de-soubeyrand.intro: A quiet crossing in the Baronnies between Sainte-Jalle and the Eygues valley. Hairpins through oaks and lavender, and usually you have the road to yourself.

sides.character: From Sainte-Jalle steadily around 6 % in hairpins through oaks and lavender; a climb with a fixed rhythm, ideal for riding up.
sides.highlights: Lavender fields in the hairpins above Sainte-Jalle.

sides.character: From Curnier in the Eygues valley longer and gentler, with calm stretches on the way; as a descent long and relaxed.

col-de-spandelles.intro: The quiet way over the ridge, an alternative to the Soulor.

sides.character: From Ferrières narrow and steadily steep through forest.
sides.highlights: The forest above the Ouzom.

sides.character: From Argelès via the villages on the slope, then narrow across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The view over the Argelès valley.

col-de-turini.intro: The Turini is famous from the night stages of the Monte Carlo Rally. Several roads meet at the top in the forest; from the east you come up the Bévéra valley from Sospel, from the west out of the Vésubie valley.

sides.character: Long and stepped: from Sospel through the narrow Piaon gorge, past Moulinet and then up through forest. Varied going down, but tight in the gorge.
sides.highlights: The Piaon gorge with the chapel of Notre-Dame-de-la-Menour.

sides.character: Shorter from La Bollène and steeper towards the top, with the stack of hairpins familiar from rally footage.
sides.highlights: The rally hairpins above La Bollène.

col-de-valberg.intro: The middle piece of the loop of the Couillole, Valberg and the red gorges.

sides.character: From Guillaumes steadily in hairpins above the Var valley.
sides.highlights: The view over the upper Var valley.

sides.character: From Beuil short and gentle across meadows.
sides.highlights: The red rocks around Beuil.

col-de-vars.intro: The Vars links the Ubaye with Guillestre and often shares a Tour de France stage with the Izoard or the Bonette. The north side runs through the ski resort of Vars, the south side is short and lonely.

sides.character: Long and stepped: from Guillestre through villages and the resort of Vars, with flatter stretches between the ramps. Downhill wide bends and open views.
sides.highlights: The Refuge Napoléon two kilometres below the top, good for a break.

sides.character: Short and open: from the Ubaye it steepens towards the top, over alpine pastures with little forest.

col-de-vence.intro: From Vence up onto a bare karst plateau above the Côte d'Azur, one of the training climbs of the pros around Nice and often part of Paris–Nice too. Short, rideable all year and with the sea at your back.

sides.character: From Vence steadily across open, stony slopes with hardly any shade. The higher you get, the further the view reaches back over the coast.
sides.highlights: The view back over the coast to the sea.

col-des-annes.intro: The pasture road above Le Grand-Bornand, a detour off the Colombière for quiet climbing.

sides.character: On the Colombière road to Le Chinaillon, then narrow and steep in hairpins across the pastures up to the plateau.
sides.highlights: The chalets of the Annes, the Pointe Percée and Mont Blanc to the south.

col-des-aravis.intro: One of the oldest Tour passes, on the programme as early as 1911 and back again and again since. Not a hard climb, but a fine one: meadows, wooden chalets and Mont Blanc facing you at the top.

sides.character: From Flumet via La Giettaz upwards in moderate steps, with flatter stretches between the ramps. Towards the top the valley opens out, green and wide.
sides.highlights: At the top the view of Mont Blanc, and cafés.

col-des-champs.intro: The Champs is the quietest link between the Verdon and the Var: narrow, mediocre tarmac, wide pastures at the top. With the Allos and the Cayolle it forms the triple loop from Barcelonnette.

sides.character: Even from Colmars in hairpins through forest up to the pastures. Quiet, but the surface needs watching either way.
Longer from the Var valley with many hairpins, steepening towards the top. Because of the surface and the tight bends, better uphill.

col-des-etroits.intro: The pass above Sainte-Croix, between Vaud and Neuchâtel.

sides.character: From Vuiteboeuf in hairpins up the slope to Sainte-Croix, then gently to the top.
sides.highlights: The view across Lake Neuchâtel.

sides.character: From Fleurier long and moderate through forest.
sides.highlights: The Val de Travers.

col-des-gets.intro: A low saddle between the Chablais and the Giffre with the ski resort of Les Gets on top. More of a passage than a goal: the Route des Grandes Alpes between Morzine and Cluses, and the way to the Joux Plane and the Ramaz.

sides.character: From Taninges gentle and even up to the turn-off for the Col de la Ramaz, then about 2 km a little steeper, flattening again before Les Gets. One stretch runs through a shady, cool gorge.
sides.highlights: The view down over the Giffre valley.

sides.character: From Morzine short and moderate on a wide road, more a link between two ski resorts than a climb. Over quickly in either direction.
sides.highlights: Les Gets itself, with the Mont Chéry above the top.

col-des-montets.intro: A low barrier between the Chamonix valley and Vallorcine, right beneath the Aiguilles Rouges. Short and never hard, but with the Mont Blanc range at your back.

sides.character: A short, even pitch up from Argentière in a few hairpins, more a crossing than a climb. At the top the high valley opens beneath the Aiguilles Rouges.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Argentière glacier and the Mont Blanc range.

col-des-mosses.intro: The broad main road from the Rhône valley into the Pays-d'Enhaut, with a high moor at the top instead of a summit. A solid, unexcited crossing that combines well with the Pillon and the Croix.

sides.character: From Le Sépey the steeper ramps come first, then it eases towards the top and the road runs out into the open moorland.

col-des-saisies.intro: At the top lies the ski resort of Les Saisies, venue of the Olympic cross-country races in 1992. As a road the pass is wide and well built, the comfortable link between the Beaufortain and the Val d'Arly.

sides.character: From Hauteluce on a wide road, the gradient switching between short steeper ramps and flatter stretches. At the top, broad alpine pastures and the ski resort.
sides.highlights: Down in Hauteluce, the church tower with the Mont Blanc massif behind it.

col-du-bonhomme.intro: The crossing from Kaysersberg to Saint-Dié on the main road, with the traffic to match. Interesting mainly as the gateway to the crest road that branches south at the top towards the Col du Calvaire and the Schlucht.

sides.character: From Lapoutroie the longer side, steepest low down, easing towards the top; as a descent even and with wide bends.
From Plainfaing short and steeper and steeper towards the top, almost without hairpins; straight ramps that are better climbed than descended.

col-du-calvaire.intro: The pass above the Lac Blanc at the northern end of the Vosges crest road. Northwards the road stays at crest height to the Col du Bonhomme; the real climb comes from Orbey.

sides.character: From Orbey steadily and almost without hairpins up through forest, at the end above the Lac Blanc; a climb with an even rhythm.
sides.highlights: The view down to the Lac Blanc beneath its rock wall.

col-du-chaussy.intro: What is famous is not the pass but its base: the Lacets de Montvernier, hairpin upon hairpin stacked into a rock face. Since the Tour discovered them in 2015 they have been among the most photographed stretches of road in the Alps; the Chaussy above remains a quiet mountain road.

sides.character: From Pontamafrey straight into the Montvernier hairpins, then steadily on past hamlets and meadows where the road turns narrow and lonely. A long, even effort with a great many hairpins.
sides.highlights: The view back down from above onto the stacked Montvernier hairpins.

col-du-coq.intro: The steep ramp from the Grenoble valley into the Chartreuse.

sides.character: From Saint-Ismier long and steep, with sections over 10 %, through forest on the flank of the Dent de Crolles.
sides.highlights: The view across the Grésivaudan to the Belledonne.

sides.character: From Saint-Pierre-de-Chartreuse steadily through forest and across pastures.
sides.highlights: The meadows below the Dent de Crolles.

col-du-corbier.intro: A short, punchy pass in the Chablais that extends a loop around Morzine to the north.

sides.character: From Le Biot short and steep all the way through forest and meadows.
sides.highlights: The view into the Vallée d'Aulps.

sides.character: From Bonnevaux a little gentler across pastures to the top.
sides.highlights: The pastures of the Corbier.

col-du-cucheron.intro: The link between the Chartreuse passes, short and through forest.

sides.character: From Saint-Pierre-d'Entremont steadily through forest and meadows.
sides.highlights: The limestone walls of the Chartreuse above the valley.

sides.character: From Saint-Pierre-de-Chartreuse short and steeper to the top.
sides.highlights: The view of the Grand Som.

col-du-galibier.intro: In the Tour de France since 1911 and often its highest point. The summit road climbs above the old tunnel, and on the south side a monument honours the Tour's founder Henri Desgrange.

sides.character: From Valloire a long moderate run up an open high valley to Plan Lachat, then it steepens through the hairpins below the top. The hard side, best saved for the climb.
sides.highlights: The hairpins from Plan Lachat, at the top the view across to the Écrins.

sides.character: Short and even from the Col du Lautaret, open and treeless, with wide views into the Écrins. A flowing, readable descent.
sides.highlights: The Desgrange monument and La Meije opposite.

col-du-glandon.intro: The Glandon lies a stone's throw from the Col de la Croix de Fer; the roads part just below the top. The north side ends with the steepest ramps, the south side passes the Grand Maison reservoir.

sides.character: Long from La Chambre: in steps through forest and pastures, with breathers on the way, and right at the end the steep ramps just before the top.
The south side goes up and down: ramps, a clear drop on the way, then along the reservoir. Heading down you have to take the counter-climb, but it is open and wide.
sides.highlights: Along the Lac de Grand Maison.

col-du-grand-saint-bernard.intro: Crossed since Roman times and by Napoleon's army in 1800; at the top stands the hospice, home of the St Bernard dogs. Since the tunnel took the traffic, the old pass road is quieter.

sides.character: From Bourg-Saint-Pierre first on the tunnel road through galleries, then on the old pass road growing steeper to the hospice.
sides.highlights: The hospice by the lake at the top.

sides.character: From Etroubles via Saint-Rhémy even up a side valley of the Aosta valley, then in hairpins near the top. A calm, flowing descent.

col-du-granier.intro: The start of every Chartreuse loop from Chambéry, with the cliff of the Granier above the top.

sides.character: From Chambéry via Montagnole steady and long up the slope, at the top below the cliff.
sides.highlights: The north face of the Mont Granier and the view over the Combe de Savoie.

sides.character: From Entremont steadily through the valley and forest to the top.
sides.highlights: The meadows of Entremont-le-Vieux.

col-du-granon.intro: A military road with no way through above Serre Chevalier, with nothing at the top but meadows and the Écrins opposite. Two Tour finishes made history: in 1986 Hinault lost the yellow jersey here, in 2022 Pogačar cracked against Vingegaard.

sides.character: From Saint-Chaffrey steep straight away and tougher still higher up, first through larches, then over open, shadeless pastures. Hardly a place to catch your breath.
sides.highlights: At the top the view of the Écrins and down into the Briançon valley

col-du-hundsruck.intro: A short wooded pass between Thann and the Doller valley at Masevaux. Useful as an approach to the Ballon d'Alsace, quiet and without much of a view.

sides.character: From Thann uneven and solid, steeper ramps alternating with easier stretches, hardly any hairpins; the harder side.
From Masevaux gentler and stepped, with hairpins and a short dip on the way; the more even side to descend.

col-du-lautaret.intro: The national road between the Oisans and Briançon is above all the approach to the Galibier, which branches off at the top. From the west you ride below the glaciers of La Meije, and there is an alpine botanical garden at the pass.

sides.character: A long valley climb in steps through the Romanche gorge with tunnels and short descents, past the Chambon reservoir and through La Grave. Because of the tunnels and the traffic, better uphill.
sides.highlights: At La Grave, La Meije and its glaciers.

sides.character: Gentle from Briançon, with no hairpins, up the Serre Chevalier valley on a wide road. Fast and clear on the way down.

col-du-marchairuz.intro: The highest pass of the Vaud Jura, with the Mollendruz a loop around the Vallée de Joux.

sides.character: From Bière steadily at around 7 % through forest, across open pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The view across Lake Geneva to the Alps.

sides.character: From the Vallée de Joux short and moderate.
sides.highlights: The Vallée de Joux.

col-du-mollard.intro: The Mollard is the quiet detour from Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne towards the Croix de Fer: long, little used and for long stretches in forest. Those who ride it usually want to spare themselves the traffic of the big passes.

sides.character: Long and in steps: from Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne up through forest and hamlets, with flatter stretches and a short descent along the way. Only at the very top does the country open out.
sides.highlights: At the top the view of the Aiguilles d'Arves.

col-du-mollendruz.intro: The second half of the loop around the Vallée de Joux.

sides.character: From Mont-la-Ville steadily through forest.
sides.highlights: The view over the Swiss plateau.

sides.character: From L'Abbaye on the Lac de Joux short and gentle.
sides.highlights: The Lac de Joux.

col-du-mont-cenis.intro: Napoleon had the road over the Mont Cenis built up; at the top a wide plateau opens with a large reservoir. A short north side from the Maurienne faces a long south ramp from Susa.

sides.character: Short from Lanslebourg, with a few wide hairpins through forest, a little steeper towards the end. Quick and clear going down.
sides.highlights: At the top the plateau opens with the lake.

sides.character: The long south ramp climbs out of the Susa valley in steps and many hairpins past hamlets, before reaching the plateau and running along the reservoir to the pass.
sides.highlights: The last kilometres along the reservoir shore.

col-du-noyer.intro: The Noyer is the balcony between the Champsaur and the Dévoluy: the road clings to a rock wall, and from the top you look out over the whole Champsaur. Little traffic, and scenically one of the great passes of the southern Western Alps.

sides.character: From Saint-Bonnet easy at first through the meadows of the Champsaur, then steeper in steps, until the final kilometres pull up the wall in hairpins.
sides.highlights: From the top the view across the whole Champsaur.

col-du-petit-ballon.intro: A bare dome with mountain inns and a view over the Munster valley and the Rhine plain, ridden on the penultimate stage of the 2023 Tour de France. Narrow, steep and quiet, the opposite of the wide roads of the big Ballons.

sides.character: From Wasserbourg steep and narrow into the forest straight away, a little easier and open over pasture towards the dome.
sides.highlights: A stop at one of the farm inns (fermes-auberges) with the view over the Munster valley.

col-du-petit-saint-bernard.intro: The Romans already used this border pass between the Tarentaise and the Aosta Valley. At the top stand a statue of St Bernard and a prehistoric stone circle, with a view of Mont Blanc's south side.

sides.character: Long and irregular from Bourg-Saint-Maurice: in hairpins up to La Rosière, then more open and varying in gradient up to the border.
sides.highlights: At La Rosière the view back down the Tarentaise.

sides.character: Shorter and even from La Thuile, in regular hairpins over pastures. Rhythmic and easy to read on the way down.
sides.highlights: The Lac Verney just before the border.

col-du-pillon.intro: The short pass between Les Diablerets and Gsteig, with the Diablerets massif and its glacier above the road. The cable car to Glacier 3000 starts at the top.

sides.character: A short, evenly steep pitch from Les Diablerets with few hairpins, the rock walls of the Diablerets always in view.
sides.highlights: The valley station of the Glacier 3000 cable car at the top.

col-du-platzerwasel.intro: A short, hard climb from the upper Munster valley onto the crest of the Vosges, in 2023 the last climb before the Tour's stage finish at the Markstein. From the south the pass lies at crest height and is no climb of its own.

sides.character: From Sondernach steep and uneven, steep ramps with few real breaks, hairpins in the forest; pastures open up on the crest at the top.
sides.highlights: At the top the crest pastures with a view into the Munster valley.

col-du-portet.intro: One of the hardest climbs in the Pyrenees, almost 1,400 m in one go.

sides.character: From Saint-Lary via Soulan to the Pla d'Adet, then narrow and steadily steep across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The Néouvielle and the lakes below the pass.

col-du-portet-d-aspet.intro: A short, steep pass with a memorial that calls for care.

sides.character: From Saint-Lary short and stiff through forest.
sides.highlights: The Couserans forests.

sides.character: From Aspet long and gentle, steep at the top past the Casartelli memorial.
sides.highlights: The Casartelli memorial.

col-du-portillon.intro: The short way from Luchon into Spain, as a loop with the Val d'Aran.

sides.character: From Luchon steadily through forest to the border.
sides.highlights: The view back to Luchon.

sides.character: From Bossòst steadily in hairpins through forest.
sides.highlights: The Val d'Aran.

col-du-pourtalet.intro: The way into Spain below the Pic du Midi d'Ossau.

sides.character: From Laruns long and moderate via Gabas and the Lac de Fabrèges.
sides.highlights: The Pic du Midi d'Ossau.

sides.character: From Sallent via Formigal steadily to the border.
sides.highlights: The Tena valley.

col-du-pre.intro: The Col du Pré is the hard, beautiful way into the Beaufortain: steeply up through forest, then the Lac de Roselend lies below you. The Tour took it in 2018 before the Cormet de Roselend.

sides.character: From Beaufort via Arêches through many hairpins in shaded forest, the ramps getting steeper rather than easier towards the top. The view only opens at the summit.
sides.highlights: From the top the Lac de Roselend seen from above, with the road to the Cormet beyond.

col-du-rousset.intro: The Rousset is the southern gateway to the Vercors: from Die the road winds up the dry southern flank, and its top is a tunnel. Beyond it the green high plateau opens up all at once.

sides.character: From Die long and gentle through the Diois, stepped with flatter sections, higher up in a run of hairpins below the cliffs to the tunnel.
sides.highlights: View from the hairpins down into the Drôme valley

col-du-sanetsch.intro: One of the longest climbs in Switzerland: from Sion over 1,700 m of climbing in one go up to the reservoir in a bare karst landscape. A dead end for bikes; the way down is the same road, or the cable car to Gsteig.

sides.character: From Sion first through vineyards and villages, then up in hairpins with a short dip on the way, and at the top through several tunnels onto the treeless plateau.
sides.highlights: The reservoir at the end, with the glaciers of the Diablerets massif above it.

col-du-somport.intro: The Way of St James pass, quiet since the tunnel.

sides.character: From Bedous long through the Vallée d'Aspe, at the top via Urdos in hairpins.
sides.highlights: The Vallée d'Aspe and the Fort du Portalet.

sides.character: From Canfranc short and gentle past the station.
sides.highlights: The Canfranc station.

col-du-soulor.intro: The pass where the Aubisque, the Spandelles and the Val d'Azun meet.

sides.character: From Arrens steadily across pastures to the pass.
sides.highlights: The Val d'Azun.

sides.character: From Ferrières through the Ouzom valley, steep in hairpins at the top.
sides.highlights: The Ouzom forests.

col-du-telegraphe.intro: Hardly anyone rides the Télégraphe for its own sake: it is the first step of the Galibier, and that is how the Tour has known it for decades. It takes its name from the old signal station, and a fort keeps watch above the top.

sides.character: From Saint-Michel-de-Maurienne almost entirely through forest, with the gradient changing more often than the figures suggest. Through the trees, repeated glimpses down into the Maurienne valley.
sides.highlights: From the top you roll down to Valloire, with the Galibier waiting beyond.

col-du-tourmalet.intro: The myth of the Pyrenees, long and steadily steep on both sides.

sides.character: From Luz through Barèges, then across the bare slopes of the Bastan valley at a steady 8 % to the top.
sides.highlights: The last hairpins below the Pic du Midi.

sides.character: From Sainte-Marie through Gripp, then steeper past the avalanche galleries and La Mongie to the top.
sides.highlights: The Arizes waterfall and the peaks above La Mongie.

col-du-wettstein.intro: A small pass between the Munster valley and Orbey, marked by the First World War: a military cemetery at the top and the Lingekopf battlefield next to it. Quiet and little used.

sides.character: From Soultzeren steadily around 6 % with a few hairpins through forest; a climb with a fixed rhythm.
sides.highlights: The military cemetery at the top.

sides.character: From Orbey longer and gentler, steady and almost without hairpins; the more relaxed side to descend.
sides.highlights: A detour to the Lingekopf battlefield.

col-saint-martin.intro: The pass where the small station of La Colmiane sits links the Vésubie with the Valdeblore. A short, friendly climb in the hinterland of Nice, which the Tour also crossed in 2020.

sides.character: From Saint-Martin-Vésubie steadily through forest, with no surprises and only a few hairpins. Good as a warm-up or as part of a bigger loop.

col-saint-roch.intro: The link between the hill villages of Lucéram and Coaraze in the hinterland of Nice. Quiet and twisting, and the piece that turns the Braus and the Turini into a loop.

sides.character: From Lucéram steadily up through a dense run of hairpins; a hairpin wall you can see from below and ride well in rhythm.
sides.highlights: Lucéram, the village on its rocky spur, at the foot.

sides.character: From Coaraze long and stepped, with a drop on the way; laborious as a climb, in the other direction a long descent with the village of Coaraze ahead.
sides.highlights: The hill village of Coaraze on its knoll.

coll-d-ordino.intro: Andorra's most beautiful pass, without the Envalira's traffic.

sides.character: From Ordino steadily steep in hairpins through forest.
sides.highlights: The view into the Ordino valley.

sides.character: From Canillo via Meritxell, moderate.
sides.highlights: The Meritxell sanctuary.

collada-de-toses.intro: The long, gentle pass into the Cerdanya.

sides.character: From Ribes long and moderate via Planoles and Toses.
sides.highlights: The hairpins above the Rigart valley.

sides.character: From Alp via La Molina steadily.
sides.highlights: The view over the Cerdanya.

colle-d-esischie.intro: A saddle between the Rocce Ciarmetta and Monte Pelvo where the road from the Vallone di Marmora meets the Fauniera road. Most riders carry on to the Colle Fauniera; the Granfondo Fausto Coppi climbs up from the Maira valley this way.

sides.character: From Ponte Marmora irregular, with a few very short ramps around 19 % and two kilometres around 10 % low down, then calmer at 6–8 % over the pastures. Long, lonely and narrow.
sides.highlights: The view back over the Marmora basin from the top.

colle-d-oggia.intro: A quiet crossing between the Argentina hinterland and Rezzo, almost car-free and rideable all year. Up from Carpasio and down to Rezzo makes a fine loop in the hinterland of the Riviera.

sides.character: From Carpasio short and evenly steep, a few hairpins and you are at the top. The climb of the loop.
Long and stepped down to Rezzo, with flatter stretches and a short counter-climb. The descent of the loop; as a climb, a long way with rests.

colle-del-lys.intro: The home climb of Turin's cyclists on the edge of the Susa valley.

sides.character: From Rubiana steadily steep through chestnut and beech forest.
sides.highlights: The view across the Susa valley and the Sacra di San Michele.

sides.character: From Viù long and gentle across pastures.
sides.highlights: The Lanzo valleys.

colle-del-melogno.intro: The home climb of Finale Ligure: from the sea through the beech woods to just over 1,000 m. A 19th-century fort stands at the top; the Calizzano side is the shorter and quieter one.

sides.character: Long and even from Finalborgo, almost at sea level, first through the hinterland, then through beech forest. The classic ascent and the side to climb.
sides.highlights: The fort at the top, and the view of the sea from the slope.

sides.character: Shorter and even from Calizzano through forest, with a few hairpins. Little traffic, calm and open as a descent.

colle-del-nivolet.intro: This dead end climbs through the Gran Paradiso National Park to over 2600 m, past the Serrù and Agnel reservoirs. In 2019 a Giro stage finished at Lago Serrù.

sides.character: Long and stepped: from Locana up the Orco valley with flatter stretches and tunnels to Ceresole Reale, then in many hairpins up to the lakes and the high valley.
sides.highlights: Lago Serrù and Lago Agnel below the last hairpins.

colle-dell-agnello.intro: The third-highest road pass in the Alps links the Varaita valley with the Queyras. In the 2016 Giro the race leader Steven Kruijswijk crashed into a snowbank on the descent here.

sides.character: From the Varaita valley very long and stepped, past the reservoir at Pontechianale, then steep and in hairpins above the treeline. The hard side, best ridden up.
sides.highlights: The Lago di Castello near Pontechianale.

sides.character: From Château-Ville-Vieille through the villages of the Queyras, steepening over wide pastures near the top. More even, and the better choice to descend.
sides.highlights: From the top a long view down into Italy.

colle-della-maddalena.intro: The lowest crossing between Cuneo and the Ubaye, the link for tours across the border.

sides.character: From Vinadio long and steady through the Valle Stura via Pietraporzio and Argentera, flatter at the top towards the lake.
sides.highlights: The cliffs of the Valle Stura and the Lago della Maddalena.

sides.character: From Larche short and moderate across pastures to the border.
sides.highlights: The wide pastures at the border.
