colle-delle-finestre.intro: On the Giro since 2005 and one of Italy's hardest climbs: tarmac below, about eight kilometres of gravel above. In 2018 Chris Froome began his solo ride to overall victory here.

sides.character: From Susa through forest in countless hairpins, with no flat stretches, then on gravel above the treeline. Long, steadily steep, and no place for thin tyres in the wet.
sides.highlights: The gravel hairpins above the treeline.

colle-di-nava.intro: The old crossing from the Riviera into the Tanaro valley, open all year. The Giro crossed it as early as 1953, and Milan–Sanremo used it in 2020 instead of the Turchino. Lavender fields at the top at almost 1,000 m.

sides.character: Even from Pieve di Teco on a wide road with barely any hairpins. The side with the height gain and the better one to climb.
From Ormea via Ponte di Nava little more than a gentle rise through the upper Tanaro valley. Undemanding uphill, a flowing run-out downhill.

colle-di-sampeyre.intro: A high, narrow crossing between the Varaita and Maira valleys, steep from both sides and hardly used. From the top the view reaches the Monviso.

sides.character: The steeper side, from Sampeyre: irregular, with few hairpins, long through forest and then over pastures. Hard uphill, a long brake downhill.
Slightly milder from the Maira valley at Stroppo, with more hairpins and also irregular. The bends make the descent easier to read.

colle-di-zambla.intro: A mid-height pass in the Bergamo valleys, the bridge between the Seriana and the Brembana.

sides.character: From Ponte Nossa steadily via Gorno and Oneta through forest.
sides.highlights: The Pizzo Arera above the top.

sides.character: From Ambria long and moderate through the Val Serina via Serina and Oltre il Colle.
sides.highlights: The villages of the Val Serina.

colle-fauniera.intro: Also called the Colle dei Morti: a narrow, high road between the Grana and Stura valleys, with the Pantani memorial at the top. The Granfondo Fausto Coppi from Cuneo crosses it.

sides.character: Long and even from Demonte up a lonely side valley, then over wide pastures. The surface is rough in either direction.
From the Grana valley it keeps steepening, the last kilometres being the hardest. Steep and rough, better up than down.
sides.highlights: The Santuario di San Magno in the upper Grana valley.

colle-gallo.intro: A low crossing between the Val Seriana and the Val Cavallina with a cyclists' chapel at the top: the sanctuary of the Madonna dei Ciclisti, Bergamo's counterpart to the Ghisallo. A training loop of the local pros.

sides.character: From Gaverina Terme short and punchy, in many hairpins and steepest at the top. The side for climbing.
From Cene in the Val Seriana long and stepped, with flat stretches and only a few hairpins. Downhill, a flowing ride into the valley.

colle-langan.intro: The crossing between the two finest valleys of the Sanremo hinterland, the Nervia valley at Pigna and the Argentina valley at Molini di Triora. Monte Toraggio stands above the top, and the road to the Colle Melosa branches off at the pass.

sides.character: From Pigna long and lonely through forest, restrained at the bottom, steeper at the top. Few hairpins, plenty of quiet: the side for going up.
sides.highlights: Monte Toraggio straight ahead at the top.

sides.character: From Molini di Triora in many hairpins that grow steeper towards the top. Shorter than the Pigna side; going down, the tight bends need attention.

colle-melosa.intro: A detour off the Colle Langan up to the Rifugio Allavena at the Colle Melosa, a good 1,500 m above the sea. One of the highest tarmac roads in the Sanremo hinterland, with views of the Ligurian Alps.

sides.character: On uphill from the Langan pass, irregular with changing ramps and only a few hairpins, more open at the top with distant views.
sides.highlights: The refuge at the end of the road for a break.

colle-san-bartolomeo.intro: A winter training climb for the pros living on the Riviera, between the Impero valley and the Arroscia valley. Olive groves, hardly any traffic and a small village at the top.

sides.character: From Chiusavecchia in hairpins through the olive groves, a little steeper towards the top. Downhill the hairpins flow well, with the valley towards the sea ahead.
sides.highlights: Downhill the view down the Impero valley towards the coast.

sides.character: From Pieve di Teco up the slope without hairpins, with a steep ramp towards the top. Better climbed than descending that steep straight.

colle-san-bernardo-di-garessio.intro: The old link from Albenga into the Tanaro valley at Garessio, open all year. Riders heading from the Riviera to the loops around Ormea and the Colle di Nava cross here.

sides.character: From Erli on the Neva a long way through chestnut forest, in steps with flatter stretches between, only a few hairpins. Flowing enough to enjoy on the way down.
From Garessio short and evenly steep in a run of hairpins. The compact climb you would rather ride up than down.

colle-san-carlo.intro: The short, hard crossing from Morgex to La Thuile averages almost ten per cent and sees little traffic. At the top the view opens onto Mont Blanc.

sides.character: A steadily steep wall out of the Aosta Valley: many hairpins through forest, no let-up. Only really a pleasure going up.
sides.highlights: The Mont Blanc view from the top.

sides.character: Short from La Thuile and also steadily steep, with few hairpins. The shorter way down.

colle-scravaion.intro: A crossing behind Albenga that is open all year, from the castle village of Castelvecchio di Rocca Barbena over to Bardineto. The loops from the Finale area over the Melogno return to the sea here.

sides.character: Evenly up from the south without hard parts, past the castle of Castelvecchio. Downhill, with the view down the valley towards the coast, the finer direction.
sides.highlights: The castle village of Castelvecchio di Rocca Barbena on its rock.

sides.character: From Bardineto barely a climb: a few gentle kilometres across the upland to the pass. The direction you ride when returning from the hinterland loops to the sea.

combe-laval.intro: One of France's boldest roads: the final kilometres are blasted as a gallery into the sheer wall of the Cirque de Combe Laval. Over the Col de la Machine it climbs into the high valley of Lente in the Vercors.

sides.character: From Saint-Jean-en-Royans unevenly up through forest, then onto the ledge in the rock wall, with tunnels and the cirque below you.
sides.highlights: The view from the gallery down into the cirque and out over the Royans

cormet-de-roselend.intro: Between the Beaufortain and the Tarentaise the Cormet passes the turquoise Lac de Roselend and climbs into a wide, bare high valley. Quiet, varied and one of the finest roads in Savoy.

sides.character: Stepped from Beaufort: through forest to the Col du Méraillet, flat along the reservoir, then up once more into the high valley. The breaks make it a lovely way up.
sides.highlights: The Lac de Roselend with its chapel on the shore.

sides.character: Even from Bourg-Saint-Maurice in hairpins through forest and open ground. Easy to read and quick on the way down.

corniche-sublime.intro: The south side of the Grand Canyon du Verdon: the road follows the rim, and from the Balcons de la Mescla you look some 250 m down onto the confluence of the Verdon and the Artuby. A day with more stops than kilometres.

sides.character: From Aiguines to Comps-sur-Artuby a long up and down along the rim of the gorge, with some hairpins and stiff counter-climbs. Hardly any net height, but a good deal more work than the figure suggests.
sides.highlights: The Balcons de la Mescla and the high bridge over the Artuby.

crans-montana.intro: The resort on the sunny terrace above Sierre. A short, steep climb straight out of the Rhône valley.

sides.character: Through the vineyards above Sierre and in hairpins from village to village, with no flat section up to the plateau.
sides.highlights: The view back across the Rhône valley to the Weisshorn and the Val d'Anniviers.

culmine-di-san-pietro.intro: The crossing from the Valsassina into the Val Taleggio, part of the Giro d'Italia more than once. Two short sides over a wooded saddle, joined into a quiet loop between Lecco and Bergamo.

sides.character: From Moggio short, steady low down and steeper above, with few hairpins through forest. The compact side, good for climbing.
From Vedeseta in the Val Taleggio steepest at the bottom, easing towards the top. The quieter side, and downhill the way into the Taleggio valley.

dientner-sattel.intro: The first of the two saddles of the Hochkönig road, with the limestone wall of the Hochkönig above the road.

sides.character: From Mühlbach steeply in hairpins through forest and over pastures up to the saddle.
sides.highlights: The south face of the Hochkönig directly above the saddle.

sides.character: From Dienten a short, moderate climb across meadows.
sides.highlights: The mountain village of Dienten with its church.

edelweissspitze.intro: A short, steep cobbled detour to the highest point of the Glockner road. At the top a wide panorama over the Hohe Tauern.

sides.character: From the Fuscher Törl steadily steep in tight cobbled hairpins up to the viewpoint. Short but demanding.
sides.highlights: A panorama of more than 30 three-thousand-metre peaks.

faschinajoch.intro: A short crossing from the Großes Walsertal to Damüls, usually ridden as the prelude to the Furkajoch. Small, but steeper from Fontanella than its height suggests.

sides.character: From Fontanella short and steep with a few hairpins, a little steeper still towards the top. The real ascent.
sides.highlights: Looking back over the Großes Walsertal.

sides.character: From Damüls a rolling link with a short descent, hardly any height. Downhill, the brief run over to Damüls.

filzensattel.intro: Together with the Dientner Sattel the crossing of the Hochkönig between the Saalach and Salzach valleys.

sides.character: From Saalfelden long and flat to Maria Alm, then moderately through the Urslau valley via Hinterthal.
sides.highlights: The walls of the Steinernes Meer above Maria Alm.

sides.character: From Dienten barely more than 3 km, but steep.
sides.highlights: The view across the Dienten basin.

flattnitz.intro: A hardly used crossing between two Carinthian valleys, ideal for a loop with the Hochrindl.

sides.character: From Glödnitz steadily through the narrow valley and over pastures.
sides.highlights: The Romanesque round church at the top.

sides.character: From Metnitz long and flat up the valley, somewhat steeper at the top.
sides.highlights: The quiet Metnitz valley.

flueelapass.intro: The Flüela links Davos with the Lower Engadin; at the top there are two small mountain lakes and the hospice. The west side climbs calmly up a wide valley, the east side from Susch is steeper.

sides.character: Mild for a long time from Davos up an open high valley, a little steeper with a few hairpins at the top. Wide and clear on the way down.
Steadily steep from Susch in hairpins, first through forest, then over open slopes. The side for climbing.
sides.highlights: The hospice by the two lakes at the top.

flumserberg.intro: A ski resort above the Walensee, an hour from Zurich and half an hour from Liechtenstein. 1,000 m in one go, made for a short day.

sides.character: From Flums straight into steep hairpins through meadows and forest, without a break up to Tannenboden.
sides.highlights: The view across the Walensee to the walls of the Churfirsten.

foppolo.intro: The detour to the end of the Brembo valley, next to the Passo San Marco.

sides.character: From Branzi via Carona in steady hairpins through forest to the resort.
sides.highlights: The head of the valley with the Orobie peaks.

forcella-aurine.intro: A quiet saddle at the foot of the Pale di San Martino, crossed by the SP347 from Agordo to Gosaldo and on to the Passo Cereda. With the Forcella Franche it makes the loop around the Gosaldo valley.

sides.character: From the Cordevole bridge near Agordo straight up at around 7 % in hairpins to Voltago, then steadily on via Frassenè; it eases near the top. A climb that is easy to pace.
sides.highlights: Frassenè beneath the walls of the Agnèr.

forcella-franche.intro: A low saddle between the Agordo basin and the wild Valle del Mis. On the south side the road runs through a narrow gorge with a reservoir and short, dark tunnels, one of the quietest corners of the Belluno Dolomites.

sides.character: From Ponte Alto near Agordo on a wide road via Rivamonte, moderately steep with a few short, harder pitches. Downhill a flowing roll-out.
sides.highlights: The view from Rivamonte over the Agordo basin.

sides.character: From Titele, where the road leaves the Mis gorge, clearly steeper in hairpins up via Tiser, narrow and with ramps up to 12 %. Coming up the valley you first ride through the unlit tunnels along the Lago del Mis.
sides.highlights: The village of Tiser and the view down into the Mis gorge.

forcola-di-livigno.intro: The high border crossing between Livigno and the Bernina area, bare and open. Usually part of the big loop over the Bernina and the Foscagno.

sides.character: Long and flat out of Livigno along the high valley, then up in steps without hairpins over bare ground to the border. Never very steep, but high and exposed to wind.

fouillouse.intro: A short, steep detour from the upper Ubaye valley to the hamlet of Fouillouse below the Chambeyron massif. On the way the road crosses the Ubaye on a high bridge.

sides.character: From the junction in the Ubaye valley stiff right away and steeper still towards the top, through a few hairpins to the hamlet. Short, but no respite.
sides.highlights: The Pont du Châtelet high above the Ubaye.

furkajoch.intro: A narrow mountain road between the Laternsertal and Damüls, little used and with an open grassy crest at the top. The view reaches to the Rätikon and the Arlberg; the west side is tight and unprotected in places.

sides.character: From Damüls short and in steps across alpine meadows, with two hairpins. The easy side, usually ridden straight after the Faschinajoch.
sides.highlights: At the top, the view to the Rätikon and the Arlberg.

sides.character: From Rankweil via Batschuns into the Laterns valley, then long and even through the valley, and from Innerlaterns narrow and steeper, in places without a crash barrier, to the top.
sides.highlights: The view back across the Rhine valley to the Swiss mountains.

furkapass.intro: James Bond filmed a car chase on the Furka for Goldfinger in 1964, and the empty Hotel Belvédère above the Rhône Glacier is still a photo stop. With the Grimsel and the Susten it makes a classic three-pass loop.

sides.character: From Realp steeper at first in hairpins, flatter near the top through an open, bare high valley. A readable descent.
From Gletsch up in hairpins, past the Hotel Belvédère, steeper near the top. Behind you lie the Grimsel hairpins.
sides.highlights: The Hotel Belvédère and the Rhône Glacier.

gaberl.intro: A long, gentle alpine pass in western Styria, a classic of the Graz cycling scene.

sides.character: From Köflach long and steady via Salla through forest up to the pastures.
sides.highlights: The open alpine domes of the Stubalpe.

sides.character: From Weißkirchen in the Mur valley steadily through forest.
sides.highlights: The view across the Aichfeld basin.

gailbergsattel.intro: A wooded saddle below 1,000 m between the Drau and the Gail that links more than it demands. Anyone riding around the Lienz Dolomites or heading for the Plöckenpass passes this way.

sides.character: From Oberdrauburg straight into the hairpins, even and never really steep up through the forest. The side with the rhythm for the climb.
sides.highlights: The view back over the Drau valley.

sides.character: From Kötschach-Mauthen flatter, with one short steep pitch and an almost level stretch before the top. Runs down into the Gail valley without surprises.
sides.highlights: The Gail valley below, with the Carnic Alps.

gaisberg.intro: A town mountain with 850 m of climbing and the all-round view from the Dachstein to the Chiemsee. In the evening after work full of road bikes.

sides.character: Out of town to Guggenthal and then steeply in hairpins through forest, at the top across the open dome of the Zistelalm to the summit.
sides.highlights: The all-round view from the summit over the Salzkammergut and the foothills.

gampenjoch.intro: The link from Meran and Lana into the Nonsberg, a pass of length rather than hairpins. From the Adige it is one of the longest steady climbs in South Tyrol; from the south hardly more than a gentle rise.

sides.character: From Lana above the orchards steadily steep almost without a break, with only a few hairpins and a wide road. The side to ride up, because it is where the work is.
sides.highlights: Looking back over the Adige valley to Meran.

sides.character: From Fondo across the high ground of the Nonsberg, even and gentle. Downhill a calm roll-out, uphill more an approach than a climb.
sides.highlights: The German-speaking villages of Unsere Liebe Frau im Walde and St. Felix along the way.

gargellen.intro: The innermost village of the Montafon, a quiet complement to the Silvretta.

sides.character: From St. Gallenkirch steadily through the narrow, wooded Gargellen valley.
sides.highlights: The Madrisa above the head of the valley.

gavarnie.intro: A gentle day to the end of the valley, with the cirque as the goal.

sides.character: From Luz through the gorge and via Gèdre gently up.
sides.highlights: The Cirque de Gavarnie at the head of the valley.

gerlitzen.intro: The viewpoint mountain above Villach and the Ossiacher See, the longest ramp around the Carinthian lakes.

sides.character: From the lakeshore long and steady via Sattendorf and the Kanzelhöhe, steeper at the top over the pastures.
sides.highlights: The view over the Ossiacher See and the Wörthersee.

gerlospass.intro: The Gerlos Alpine Road links the Zillertal with the upper Pinzgau, past the Durlassboden reservoir. On the Krimml side you look across to the Krimml Waterfalls, Austria's highest. A lot of traffic, but a gentle gradient.

sides.character: From Zell am Ziller first in hairpins out of the valley, then long and flatter through the Gerlos valley and along the reservoir. Stepped and long, the climb with a run-up.
From Krimml shorter, in wide hairpins above the Salzach valley with the waterfalls opposite. Descending, the view is ahead of you.
sides.highlights: View of the Krimml Waterfalls

glaubenberg.intro: The quiet neighbour of the Glaubenbielen, from Sarnen into the Entlebuch. Long ramps through forest, moorland at the top and hardly any traffic even in summer.

sides.character: From Sarnen the steep ramps through the forest come first; in the upper part it eases and the road runs out into the moorland.

glaubenbielen.intro: The panoramic road from Giswil up to Sörenberg, across wide alpine pastures beneath the Brienzer Rothorn. Long, steep and quiet in summer, a classic of Central Switzerland.

sides.character: Long and even up from the Sarnersee, a little steeper still towards the top. Forest below, open pastures above with a view back over the lake.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Sarnersee, the Brienzer Rothorn at the top.

goldeck-panoramastrasse.intro: One of the hardest roads in Carinthia, up to a viewpoint summit above the Drau valley.

sides.character: From Spittal steeply through forest and in hairpins over the pastures, hardly a stretch below 8 % up to the car park below the summit.
sides.highlights: The all-round view from the Goldeck over the Drau valley and the Millstätter See.

gorges-de-daluis.intro: The red canyon of the upper Var, often compared with the Colorado: the road runs on galleries and through tunnels high above the water. Hardly any gradient, but uninterrupted scenery.

sides.character: From Daluis to Guillaumes an up and down with no real net gain, across galleries and through short tunnels. More looking than climbing.
sides.highlights: The Pont de la Mariée high above the gorge.

gorges-de-la-bourne.intro: The road through the Bourne gorge is blasted into the rock wall for kilometres, single-track in places beneath overhanging rock. It links Pont-en-Royans with Villard-de-Lans and is one of the main approaches to the Vercors.

sides.character: From Pont-en-Royans upstream through the gorge, stepped and mostly gentle, with short steeper pitches, tunnels and rock overhangs, up onto the plateau at Villard-de-Lans.
sides.highlights: The houses hanging over the river at Pont-en-Royans, at the start

gorges-de-la-nesque.intro: A balcony road that climbs almost imperceptibly, opposite the rock mass of the Rocher du Cire. The scenic way from the Carpentras side to Sault and so to the foot of the Ventoux.

sides.character: From Villes-sur-Auzon to Sault a long, gentle rise along the gorge wall, with steps and a descent in between. Not a climb for suffering, but one for looking.
sides.highlights: The viewpoint opposite the Rocher du Cire.

gorges-du-cians.intro: One of the most impressive gorges of the Maritime Alps: in the upper part red schist almost closes over the road, with narrow tunnels in between. It leads from the Var up to Beuil, the gateway to Valberg.

sides.character: From Touët-sur-Var flat to moderate for a long way through the gorge, with steps and a short descent. Grey rock lower down, red schist higher up, before the final climb to Beuil.
sides.highlights: The narrowest point in the red schist, where the walls almost meet above the road.

gorges-du-guil.intro: The Combe du Queyras is the gateway to the Queyras: a road on galleries and through tunnels above the Guil. Where it emerges from the gorge at the top, the Izoard and the Agnel branch off.

sides.character: From Guillestre up the gorge in gentle steps, with the occasional descent along the way. More a long approach to the big passes than a climb in its own right.
sides.highlights: At the end of the gorge the fort of Château-Queyras on its rock.

gorges-du-nan.intro: Cut into the wall in 1894 without a parapet, the road through the Gorges du Nan is among the wildest in the Vercors. Three short unlit tunnels, nothing but air below, and hardly any traffic.

sides.character: Up from Cognin-les-Gorges with a changing, at times stiff gradient, until the road hangs in the wall as a narrow ribbon. Up to Malleval, from where it carries on towards the Col du Mont Noir.
sides.highlights: The ledge cut into the rock, without a parapet, high above the Nan.

gotthard-tremola.intro: The cobbled Tremola on the Ticino side is one of the finest hairpin roads in the Alps, built in the 19th century. Since the tunnel and the new road arrived, it belongs almost entirely to cyclists.

sides.character: From Airolo on the Tremola's cobbles, hairpin after hairpin at an even gradient up the gorge. A treat going up, bumpy going down.
sides.highlights: The Tremola's granite-paved hairpins.

sides.character: From Hospental on the modern road, even and with few hairpins up an open high valley. Wide and smooth, the side for the descent.

grand-ballon.intro: The highest point of the Vosges that a road reaches, and on the Tour de France route several times. At the top a wide view over the Rhine plain and the Black Forest, on a clear day as far as the Alps; the summit with its radar dome is a few minutes on foot.

sides.character: From Willer-sur-Thur long in the forest, steadily steeper towards the top, with hairpins in the last third; at the end you leave the trees for the bare dome.
sides.highlights: Leaving the forest for the open dome and its all-round view.

sides.character: From Uffholtz the long side, stepped with easier stretches and a dip, past the Hartmannswillerkopf and then along the crest road; as a descent long and varied.
sides.highlights: The First World War memorial at the Hartmannswillerkopf (Vieil Armand).

grand-colombier.intro: The hardest climb in the Jura, almost 1,250 m from the Rhône valley with ramps over 10 %.

sides.character: From Culoz first in hairpins above the Rhône valley, then through forest with the steepest ramps over 10 % and finally across the open pastures.
sides.highlights: The view over the Lac du Bourget and the Rhône valley.

sides.character: From Anglefort the most direct and irregularly steep through forest, the hardest side.
sides.highlights: The view down to the Rhône.

sides.character: From the Valromey short and brutally steep, with sections around 12 %.
sides.highlights: The villages of the Valromey.

grimselpass.intro: Granite, reservoirs and the stack of hairpins above Gletsch define the Grimsel. Together with the Furka and the Susten it makes one of Switzerland's best-known pass loops.

sides.character: From Innertkirchen a long climb up the Haslital, with a changing gradient, through galleries and past the reservoirs in the granite landscape. A long, flowing descent.
sides.highlights: The Räterichsboden and Grimsel reservoirs.

sides.character: From Gletsch a short climb up a staircase of hairpins, flatter near the top. The hairpins lie in plain view ahead and are fun to climb.
sides.highlights: The Totensee at the top.

grosse-scheidegg.intro: Closed to cars, with only the PostBus running: the Grosse Scheidegg is a quiet mountain road between Meiringen and Grindelwald. At the top you stand right below the Wetterhorn and the Eiger.

sides.character: From Meiringen past the Reichenbach Falls up the Reichenbach valley via Rosenlaui and Schwarzwaldalp, irregular with steep pitches. Long, quiet and varied.
sides.highlights: The Reichenbach Falls near Meiringen.

sides.character: From Grindelwald steep over open pasture, steeper near the top. As a descent the Eiger and the Wetterhorn are ahead of you, but it is narrow with oncoming PostBuses.
sides.highlights: The Eiger north face opposite.

grossglockner-hochalpenstrasse.intro: Opened in 1935 and still Austria's best-known scenic road, with views of the country's highest mountain. A long high-mountain crossing with two detours, to the Edelweißspitze and the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe.

sides.character: From Fusch very long and stepped, in hairpins via Hochmais to the Fuscher Törl and with a short dip before the Hochtor. Wide and well built, a long, quick descent.
sides.highlights: The turn-off to the Edelweißspitze at the Fuscher Törl.

sides.character: From Heiligenblut steeper, in hairpins over open slopes, with the Großglockner in view. The shorter, harder side for climbing.
sides.highlights: The pilgrimage church of Heiligenblut against the Glockner.

gurnigelpass.intro: The highest pass in the Bernese Prealps and the home climb of the cyclists of Bern and Thun.

sides.character: From Wattenwil steeply in hairpins up the slope, then steadily through forest to Gurnigelbad and across the moors to the top.
sides.highlights: The view across the Swiss plateau and at the top the four-thousanders of the Bernese Oberland.

sides.character: From Zollhaus through the valley of the Kalte Sense, moderate and quiet up to the Selibühl.
sides.highlights: The Gantrisch ridge above the valley.

haggenegg.intro: The steepest road around the Mythen, with Lake Lucerne below.

sides.character: Steep right from Schwyz via Rickenbach, then long ramps over pastures up to the saddle below the Kleiner Mythen.
sides.highlights: The view of the Mythen and down to Lake Lucerne.

hahntennjoch.intro: The Hahntennjoch links Imst with the Lech valley, its south side running through bare scree slopes. Popular with motorcyclists; since 2020 particularly loud machines have been banned.

sides.character: From the Lech valley via Bschlabs: up first, then some height is lost before the real climb leads in hairpins to the pass. Stepped and varied; as a descent it includes a climb back up.
From Imst the steep side, uneven with ramps, higher up through open scree slopes with a clear view back. A wall to ride uphill.
sides.highlights: View back into the Inn valley and onto the Lechtal Alps

hautacam.intro: A hard Tour climb with changing gradients and a view over the Lourdes valley.

sides.character: From Argelès via Ayros, then with changing ramps over 10 % through forest and pastures to the resort.
sides.highlights: The view over the Lavedan.

haute-vallee-de-cervieres.intro: A gentle detour off the Izoard's north side into a remote high valley. Little traffic and wide pastures, more of a cruise than a climb.

sides.character: Up the valley from Cervières in steps, mostly flat, with a few short ramps and small dips. Open country without any rush.

hintertux.intro: The Tuxertal ends below Austria's only year-round glacier ski area. A valley climb with a steep start out of Mayrhofen.

sides.character: Steep in hairpins out of Mayrhofen to Finkenberg, then more evenly through the Tuxertal via Lanersbach to Hintertux.
sides.highlights: The glacier at the head of the valley above the hotels of Hintertux.

hochkar.intro: The Hochkar Alpenstraße is a short, very steep toll road in the limestone Alps of Lower Austria. At the ski area on top the view reaches across the Ybbstal Alps to the Ötscher.

sides.character: Double-digit steep from Lassing right away and if anything harder towards the top, with few hairpins. A climb to grit your teeth through; going down means a lot of braking.
sides.highlights: At the top the view across the Ybbstal Alps to the Ötscher.

hochrindl.intro: The crossing onto the pastures of the Gurktal Alps, at the top open space and stone pines.

sides.character: From Sirnitz steeply through forest in hairpins.
sides.highlights: The pastures of the Hochrindl.

sides.character: From Ebene Reichenau steady and gentler.
sides.highlights: The view to the Nock mountains.

hochsoelden.intro: A short, steep detour off the glacier road up to the hotel hamlet of Hochsölden on a terrace high above the Ötztal. Only a few kilometres, but hardly ever below 10 %.

sides.character: Steep straight away from the junction, with a run of hairpins on the slope; it eases a little towards the end.
sides.highlights: View down onto Sölden and across to the peaks of the Ötztal Alps

hochtannbergpass.intro: The crossing from the Bregenzerwald into the Lechtal, between Widderstein and Braunarlspitze. Short but high and open, with galleries against the avalanches on the slopes above.

sides.character: From Schröcken steadily steep through a few hairpins and galleries, a compact climb with views back into the valley. The side with character to ride up.
sides.highlights: The Widderstein above the top of the pass.

sides.character: From Warth short and gentle, only a little steeper towards the top, no hairpins across open meadows. Downhill a calm finish towards the Lechtal.

hohneck.intro: A spur road from the Route des Crêtes to just below one of the highest summits of the Vosges. At the top a view over the crest, the cirque lakes and on clear days far into the Rhine plain.

sides.character: From La Bresse long and stepped through forest onto the crest, with hairpins and easier sections, at the end over open pasture to the summit area.
sides.highlights: The all-round view from the Hohneck over the crest and the lakes.

hourquette-d-ancizan.intro: The Aspin's little brother, narrow and almost traffic-free.

sides.character: From Ancizan narrow and steep through forest, across pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The pastures below the Arbizon.

sides.character: From Payolle gently across the Campan pastures.
sides.highlights: The open pastures.

ibergeregg.intro: The short crossing between Schwyz and the Sihltal, with the rock teeth of the Mythen as constant companions. Open all year and only a short climb from Oberiberg.

sides.character: A short stretch over pastures from Oberiberg, moderate at first and a little steeper towards the end, with only a few hairpins.
sides.highlights: The Mythen in view at the top.

iffigenalp.intro: A quiet dead end at the head of the Simmental, past waterfalls to a mountain inn.

sides.character: From Lenk first flat, then single-lane and steep through forest along the Iffigbach.
sides.highlights: The Iffig waterfall beside the road.

iselsberg.intro: The saddle between East Tyrol and Carinthia that carries the Glockner road up from Lienz: anyone riding from Lienz to the Grossglockner climbs it here, and again from the other side on the way back. At the top a village with inns and the view of the Lienz Dolomites.

sides.character: From Dölsach steady at around 7 % with a few hairpins, open and with little shade; the Iselsberg village sign comes before the top, and the road climbs on a little after it.
sides.highlights: The view back over the Lienz basin to the Lienz Dolomites.

sides.character: From Winklern short and evenly steep, around 8 % nearly all the way, easing only over the last few hundred metres.
sides.highlights: The view up the Möll valley towards Heiligenblut.

jaufenpass.intro: The Jaufen links the Passeier valley with Sterzing and is the third pass of the Ötztaler Radmarathon, ridden from Sterzing. Popular with motorcyclists; open pastures and views of the Texel group on the south side.

sides.character: From St. Leonhard steady and long, through forest and then in many hairpins over the sunny southern slopes. A rhythm that carries you uphill.
From Sterzing through the Jaufental, stepped with flatter stretches and few hairpins, mostly in forest. The Ötztaler direction; as a descent the faster side.

jaunpass.intro: The crossing from the Simmental into the Gruyère country, over the language border from German into French. A quiet, even pre-Alpine pass through forest and pasture.

sides.character: From Boltigen through forest and pasture, with a number of hairpins and getting a little steeper towards the top. A climb for riding a rhythm.

jochgrimm.intro: The short extension from the Lavazè pass up to just under 2,000 m, below the Schwarzhorn and the Weißhorn. More reward than climb: the view reaches far across the Adige valley and the Dolomites.

sides.character: From the junction on the Lavazè pass evenly and moderately steep across alpine pasture, almost without hairpins. An encore that costs hardly any effort.
sides.highlights: At the top the Schwarzhorn and Weißhorn directly above the road.

julierpass.intro: The Romans already crossed the Julier, and remains of a column still stand at the top. From the north a long climb up the Surses past the Marmorera reservoir, from Silvaplana short and direct.

sides.character: Long and stepped from Tiefencastel, with flatter stretches through the villages and along the reservoir, then hairpins over bare ground at the top.
sides.highlights: Along the Marmorera reservoir.

sides.character: Short from Silvaplana, steepest at the start and flatter higher up, with hardly a hairpin. On the way down the Engadin lakes lie ahead.
sides.highlights: The view over the Upper Engadin lakes.

kaiser-franz-josefs-hoehe.intro: The Gletscherstraße ends at the visitor centre facing the Großglockner, high above the Pasterze, Austria's longest glacier. A detour busy with day-trippers, best early in the day.

sides.character: From the Guttal in steps with a short dip, moderately steep over pasture, then along the slope to the end of the road.
sides.highlights: The Großglockner and the Pasterze straight opposite.

kals-lucknerhaus.intro: The Kalser Glocknerstraße runs up the Ködnitz valley to the Lucknerhaus, right beneath the Großglockner. From the end of the road the south side of Austria's highest mountain stands directly above the valley head.

sides.character: Evenly steep from Kals up the Ködnitz valley, with few hairpins and hardly a flatter spot. The Glockner draws ever closer as you go.
sides.highlights: At the Lucknerhaus the Großglockner straight ahead.

kartitscher-sattel.intro: An open meadow saddle between the Lienz Dolomites and the Carnic ridge, where the Gail flows east and the Gailbach west. It links the Pustertal with the Lesachtal and is part of the loop around the Lienz Dolomites.

sides.character: From Tassenbach with the steeper ramps and the hairpins up to Kartitsch, then flatter across the meadows to the saddle. The side that asks something of the climb.
sides.highlights: The village of Kartitsch below the Carnic ridge.

sides.character: From Untertilliach gentle and long beside the young Gail through Obertilliach, with short rollers in between. Downhill a long roll through the upper Lesachtal.
sides.highlights: Obertilliach and its compact village centre.

katschberg.intro: A short, brutal pass between Salzburg and Carinthia, with a ski resort at the top. Six kilometres that feel like a big mountain.

sides.character: From St. Michael straight and very steep up the slope, hardly a hairpin to catch one's breath.
sides.highlights: The view back across the Lungau.

sides.character: From Rennweg just as short and steep, with a few hairpins.
sides.highlights: The Lieser valley towards Gmünd.

kaunertaler-gletscherstrasse.intro: One of the highest roads in Austria: from the Kaunertal past the Gepatsch reservoir up into the glacier world of the Ötztal Alps. Toll-free for bikes, and for the legs one of the hardest climbs in the Eastern Alps.

sides.character: First a long way along the valley floor and the reservoir with flatter sections, then in the upper part a dense run of hairpins above the tree line in thin air.
sides.highlights: The Gepatsch reservoir, and the glaciers in view at the top.

kesselberg.intro: The hairpin road between the Kochelsee and the Walchensee was long the scene of hill climb races and is still a magnet for motorcyclists, correspondingly loud on fine weekends. Short, but the view of the Walchensee carries it.

sides.character: From Kochel flat along the lake at first, then up the Kesselberg in a tight series of hairpins, getting steeper towards the top. Short and twisty, most pleasant on weekdays.
sides.highlights: The Walchensee power station at the start, the view of the Walchensee at the top.

kitzbueheler-horn.intro: A steep dead end from Kitzbühel up the town's own mountain, a regular summit finish of the Tour of Austria. At the top a wide view over the Kitzbühel Alps to the Wilder Kaiser.

sides.character: From Kitzbühel in steps, very steep ramps between short breathers and many hairpins over pasture. Hard all the way.
sides.highlights: The view to the Wilder Kaiser.

klausenpass.intro: Between 1922 and 1934 the Klausen hill climb for cars was held here. The pass links Uri with Glarus, with the wide Urnerboden on its eastern side.

sides.character: From Altdorf long up the Schächental, stepped with flatter sections and steeper pitches, open slopes near the top. A long, quick descent.
From Linthal steeply up in hairpins, then flat across the Urnerboden and finally in hairpins below rock walls to the top. Varied and good for climbing.
sides.highlights: The Urnerboden, Switzerland's largest alpine pasture.

klippitztoerl.intro: A rounded alpine pass in the east of Carinthia, opposite the Koralpe with the Weinebene.

sides.character: From Bad St. Leonhard steadily through forest up to the pastures.
sides.highlights: The view across the Lavant valley.

sides.character: From Lölling through the Lölling valley, moderate and quiet.
sides.highlights: The old mining villages of the Görtschitz valley.

kolm-saigurn.intro: A valley head in the Hohe Tauern national park, ringed by three-thousanders. A quiet alternative to the big Tauern roads.

sides.character: From Rauris long and flat via Wörth and Bucheben, steeper at the end up to the pastures of Kolm-Saigurn.
sides.highlights: The head of the valley with the Sonnblick and its waterfalls.

kuehtai.intro: The crossing from the Ötztal into the Sellrain valley is the first climb of the Ötztaler Radmarathon, ridden from Ötz. At the top sits the ski village of Kühtai at just over 2000 m, reachable all year.

sides.character: From Kematen long and without hairpins up the Sellrain valley, a steady rise with a few steeper pitches higher up. As a descent long and flowing, as in the Ötztaler.
From Ötz the steeper side: uneven, ramps through forest and a few hairpins, more open higher up. The marathon direction and the better way up.

l-ecot.intro: A short dead end from Bonneval-sur-Arc to the stone hamlet of L'Écot at the very head of the Haute Maurienne. A quiet extra at the end of an Iseran ride.

sides.character: Up the valley beside the young Arc without hairpins, steepening towards the hamlet. Little traffic, open meadows and glacier views.
sides.highlights: The old stone houses of L'Écot.

la-plagne.intro: In 2025 the ski resort above the Tarentaise was the finish of stage 19 of the Tour de France, won by Thymen Arensman just ahead of Vingegaard and Pogačar, and that same summer the finish of the Étape du Tour for amateurs. The road was built for winter sport: wide, steady and with many hairpins.

sides.character: From Aime via Mâcot almost all the way at 7 to 8 %, in long series of hairpins through the forest; near the top it eases briefly between the ski stations before climbing once more from Plagne Centre to Plagne Villages.
sides.highlights: The view back down the Isère valley and to the peaks of the Tarentaise once the forest ends.

la-planche-des-belles-filles.intro: A Tour de France finish since 2012, and in 2020 the scene of the time trial with which Pogačar won the Tour. A short, hard climb in the forest that gets steeper and steeper towards the top.

sides.character: From Plancher-les-Mines moderate at first, then steeper and steeper in the forest up to the ski station; the hardest metres come at the end.
sides.highlights: The Tour's finishing straight at the ski station.

la-toussuire.intro: The Maurienne's Tour climb, which joins the Mollard to make a loop.

sides.character: From Saint-Jean in hairpins via Fontcouverte, then steadily across meadows to the resort.
sides.highlights: The view of the Aiguilles d'Arves.

lac-de-cap-de-long.intro: The highest paved road in the Hautes-Pyrénées after the Tourmalet, up to a reservoir.

sides.character: From Saint-Lary gently to Fabian, then steep in hairpins past the Lac d'Orédon to the dam.
sides.highlights: The Lac d'Orédon and the Néouvielle.

lac-de-moiry.intro: The highest road in the Val d'Anniviers ends on the crest of a dam, with the glacier at the far end of the lake. One of the great climbs of the Valais, and one of the quietest.

sides.character: At the bottom the valley road into the Val d'Anniviers, in hairpins and along the rock face; quieter from Vissoie, and from Grimentz narrow, steep and above the tree line up to the dam.
sides.highlights: The village of Grimentz with its old granaries, and at the top the view across the lake to the glacier.

le-chazelet.intro: A short dead end above La Grave that ends at the oratory, directly opposite the Meije and its glaciers. One of the great panoramas of the Western Alps, earned with only a few metres of climbing.

sides.character: From La Grave up a tight run of hairpins, a little steeper towards the top, with the Meije behind you and finally before your eyes.
sides.highlights: The Meije from the oratory at the edge of Le Chazelet

le-markstein.intro: The Markstein is the hub of the southern High Vosges: the crest road, the Florival and the upper Thur valley meet here, and the Tour de France keeps coming by, climbing from Linthal in 2014 and finishing here in 2023. At the top meadows, ski lifts and inns, with the Grand Ballon close by on the crest road.

sides.character: From Lautenbach up the Florival gently at first, then in two steeper sections through the forest, split by the flat stretch at the Lac de la Lauch; the last kilometres pick up once more.
sides.highlights: The Lac de la Lauch halfway up, a reservoir in the forest below the crest.

sides.character: From Wildenstein at the head of the Thur valley quiet and steady in hairpins through the forest, topping out on open meadows just above the station before dropping gently to it.
sides.highlights: The view over the Kruth-Wildenstein reservoir on the way up.

lenzerheide.intro: The crossing from the Chur Rhine valley into the Albula valley, over a high valley with lakes and holiday villages. Not a quiet pass, but the way from Chur to the great passes of Graubünden.

sides.character: Steeply out of Chur in hairpins to Malix, then evenly through Churwalden and Parpan up to the high valley.
sides.highlights: The Heidsee between Valbella and Lenzerheide.

sides.character: From Tiefencastel via Lantsch in long loops along the slope, even and with a wide view into the Albula valley; flowing as a descent.
sides.highlights: The view across the Albula valley to the church of Tiefencastel.

les-arcs.intro: The ski-resort ascent from Bourg-Saint-Maurice via Arc 1800 up to Arc 2000. In the 1996 Tour, Miguel Indurain cracked in the final kilometres to Les Arcs; his run of five Tour wins ended that year.

sides.character: From Bourg-Saint-Maurice stepped with many hairpins through forest and meadows, then up between the ski stations, with steeper ramps in between.
sides.highlights: View across the upper Tarentaise valley

les-deux-alpes.intro: The Oisans's second resort climb, steady in hairpins.

sides.character: From the Chambon reservoir via Mont-de-Lans in steady hairpins to the resort.
sides.highlights: The Lac du Chambon and the Meije to the east.

leukerbad.intro: The road to the largest spa town in the Alps, on a rock face above the Dala gorge. An even climb with an ending one does not forget: the sheer Gemmi wall above the village.

sides.character: From Susten in hairpins through Leuk, then evenly along the slope above the gorge, with no steep sections, up to the village.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Dala gorge and the Gemmi wall at the head of the valley.

loiblpass.intro: Traffic takes the tunnel that prisoners of the Loibl concentration camp sub-camp were forced to build; the old road over the top stays quiet and steep. The border between Carinthia and Slovenia runs across the top.

sides.character: From Ferlach a long way up the Loibl valley, in steps with a descent on the way, then a few very steep ramps on the old pass road at the top. A long run-up to a hard finish.
sides.highlights: The memorial to the concentration camp sub-camp at the northern tunnel portal.

sides.character: From Tržič increasingly steep, on the old road at the top through hairpins and steep ramps. Shorter than the north side, similarly hard at the finish.

loser-panoramastrasse.intro: The toll road up the Loser is short but one of the steepest climbs in the Salzkammergut. The Altausseer See lies below, the plateau on the edge of the Totes Gebirge above, with the view across the Ausseerland.

sides.character: Steep from Altaussee right away, hairpins up the slope, steeper still towards the top. Hardly a breather, but more of the lake with every metre.
sides.highlights: The Altausseer See far below, the Totes Gebirge at the top.

luenersee.intro: A valley head in the Rätikon below the walls of the Schesaplana, the quietest ramp around Bludenz.

sides.character: From Bludenz in hairpins via Bürserberg into the Brandnertal, moderate up to Brand, then narrow and steep to the valley station.
sides.highlights: The limestone walls of the Schesaplana at the head of the valley.

lukmanierpass.intro: One of the gentlest Alpine crossings in Switzerland: from the Vorderrhein at Disentis into the Blenio valley in Ticino, past the Sontga Maria reservoir at the top. Little traffic, lots of space.

sides.character: From Disentis through the Medel gorge with tunnels, then in steps with a small dip up the wide Val Medel. Long and flowing on the way down.
sides.highlights: The gorge of the Medel Rhine beyond Disentis.

sides.character: Irregular from Olivone: steeper pieces in the lower part, then calmer up the upper Blenio valley to the top.
sides.highlights: The Sontga Maria reservoir at the top.

luz-ardiden.intro: The second resort climb above Luz, with textbook hairpins.

sides.character: From Luz via Sazos steadily, at the top in tight hairpins across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The hairpins below the resort.

macugnaga.intro: A long valley road to the east side of the Monte Rosa, where the face rises 2,500 metres above the village. Not a hard climb, but a destination.

sides.character: From Piedimulera first steeper in hairpins out of the Ossola valley, then long and even high above the Anza through chestnut forest and villages.
sides.highlights: The east face of the Monte Rosa, which appears at the head of the valley beyond Ceppo Morelli.

madonna-del-colletto.intro: A low crossing over the ridge between the Valle Stura and the Valle Gesso, with the Santuario Madonna del Colletto at the top. Known as the final climb of the Granfondo Fausto Coppi, which rides up from Festiona and down to Valdieri.

sides.character: From Festiona through forest, with several ramps above 12 % in the first half, then steadier. Old, uneven tarmac with grit, the better choice uphill.
sides.highlights: The little church on the saddle.

sides.character: From Valdieri shorter and steep throughout, in hairpins above the Gesso valley, with a stretch of concrete near the top. The Granfondo descends this way.
sides.highlights: The view over the Gesso valley out towards Cuneo.

madonna-del-ghisallo.intro: Not a high pass but a place of pilgrimage for cycling: since 1949 the Madonna del Ghisallo has been the patron saint of cyclists, and the cycling museum stands beside the chapel. The climb from Bellagio is a fixture of the Giro di Lombardia.

sides.character: Steep from Bellagio right away in hairpins above Lake Como, then a flatter stretch through Civenna and a last short rise to the chapel.
sides.highlights: The chapel with the champions' jerseys and bikes, the view over Lake Como.

malbun.intro: The one big climb of a whole country. More than 1,100 m in 13 kilometres, from the capital to the end of the road.

sides.character: From Vaduz steeply in hairpins up the slope to Triesenberg, through the tunnel into the Samina valley to Steg, and from there steep once more to Malbun.
sides.highlights: The view from Triesenberg across the Rhine valley to the Churfirsten and the Alpstein.

malojapass.intro: The Maloja is only a pass on one side: from Chiavenna the Bregaglia climbs long, and at the top the road runs almost level into the Upper Engadin. The wall of hairpins right at the top is its trademark.

sides.character: Long and stepped up the Bregaglia via Castasegna and Vicosoprano with flatter stretches, finishing with the tight wall of hairpins below the top.
sides.highlights: Lake Sils just beyond the top.

malta-hochalmstrasse.intro: The toll road runs through the Malta valley, known for its waterfalls, up to the Kölnbrein dam, Austria's highest. On the way, waterfalls and narrow tunnels controlled by traffic lights.

sides.character: From Gmünd long and flat up the Malta valley, then stepped and steeper in hairpins and through tunnels up to the dam wall.
sides.highlights: The Kölnbrein dam and its reservoir in the Hohe Tauern

mangart-sattel.intro: Slovenia's highest road was built as an Italian military road in the 1930s. With unlit tunnels and narrow ramps it climbs beneath the north faces of the Mangart, one of the wildest dead ends in the Eastern Alps.

sides.character: From Log pod Mangartom first towards the Predel, then onto the narrow mountain road: stepped, long stretches at 8 % and more, with hairpins, tunnels and ever wider views.
sides.highlights: The rock walls of the Mangart and the view across the Julian Alps

martelltal.intro: From the Vinschgau up beneath the glaciers of the Cevedale: a dead end with 1,400 m of climbing. In 2013 a Giro stage was due to finish here and was cancelled for snow; otherwise the valley is known for its strawberries.

sides.character: From Goldrain a long moderate run into the valley with flat steps, then hairpins up to the Zufrittsee and a steep final section to the Enzianhütte. The climb gets harder towards the end.
sides.highlights: The Zufrittsee and, at the top, the north faces of the Cevedale.

melchsee-frutt.intro: The highest road in central Switzerland ends at a mountain lake. The finish from Stöckalp is one of the steepest ramps in Switzerland.

sides.character: From Kerns steadily through the Melchtal to Stöckalp, then narrow and very steep in hairpins up to the plateau.
sides.highlights: The Melchsee on the plateau.

mendelpass.intro: Kaltern's home mountain: out of the vineyards and up the Mendel wall in hairpins, with the Adige valley and the Dolomites behind you. Alongside the road the Mendelbahn, one of the steepest funiculars in Europe, runs to the top.

sides.character: From Kaltern evenly up the wall in many tight hairpins, each ramp visible ahead. A fine rhythm uphill; downhill, with traffic, rather hard work.
sides.highlights: Looking back over the Kalterer See and the Adige valley to the Rosengarten.

sides.character: From the Nonsberg at Sarnonico short, with a flat step on the way, almost without hairpins. Not much as a climb, pleasant as the way down into the Nonsberg.

meribel-mottaret.intro: A gentle detour off the Loze climb through Méribel to the ski village of Mottaret. More a link than a climb.

sides.character: From Méribel up the valley in steps, mostly moderate, with short dips between the village parts. Ski-resort scenery rather than wilderness.

mont-crosin.intro: The opposite slope to the Chasseral, short and steep from Saint-Imier.

sides.character: From Saint-Imier short and steep through forest.
sides.highlights: The view of the Chasseral.

sides.character: From Tramelan gently across the pastures of the Franches-Montagnes.
sides.highlights: The pastures and wind turbines.

mont-du-chat.intro: One of the hardest climbs between the Jura and the Alps, with the lake at its feet.

sides.character: From the lakeshore without a break at around 9 % through forest, hardly any respite until the top.
sides.highlights: The Lac du Bourget below the road.

sides.character: From Yenne long and steadier through villages and forest.
sides.highlights: The view into the Rhône valley.

mont-revard.intro: The long forest climb from the Lac du Bourget onto the Bauges plateau.

sides.character: From Aix-les-Bains via Mouxy steady and long through forest, flatter across the plateau at the top to the viewpoint.
sides.highlights: The view from the Revard over the Lac du Bourget.

mont-ventoux.intro: The Giant of Provence stands alone above the plain, its bare limestone summit visible from far away. On the Tour since 1951; Tom Simpson died here in 1967. Three ascents, all with the wind as an opponent.

sides.character: From Bédoin gentle at first, then long and steep through the forest to Chalet Reynard, then across the scree towards the summit tower. The classic climb.
sides.highlights: The Tom Simpson memorial just below the summit.

sides.character: From Malaucène the steepest side, with hard pitches in the forest. As a descent wide and fast, with few hairpins.
sides.highlights: The view across to the Dentelles de Montmirail.

sides.character: From Sault the gentlest side, long and stepped through lavender fields and forest, joining the Bédoin road at Chalet Reynard for the summit.
sides.highlights: The lavender fields around Sault.

montagne-de-lure.intro: The long, quiet climb of Haute-Provence, the Ventoux without the crowds.

sides.character: From Saint-Étienne steadily through oak and beech forest, at the top across the bare ridge.
sides.highlights: The panorama from the ridge over Provence and the Alps.

monte-beigua.intro: The highest summit of the Beigua massif, barely 15 km as the crow flies from the beach: from Varazze you climb from sea level to almost 1,300 m. Antennas and wind at the top, and a view that on clear days reaches from the sea to the Alps.

sides.character: Up from the sea via Alpicella, moderate at first, then ever steeper, with the hardest ramps in the upper part. With the sea at your back, the climb you come here for.
sides.highlights: The view back over the coast and the Gulf of Genoa.

sides.character: From Sassello in the hinterland, long and in steps across the upland, with some height given back on the way. Quiet and rarely steep, the pleasanter side for rolling down inland.

monte-bignone.intro: Sanremo's home mountain and one of the longest ascents on the Riviera dei Fiori: from the harbour in one go to over 1,000 m. The tarmac ends just below the summit.

sides.character: From the sea through the villa districts, then up in hairpins via San Romolo; it steepens towards the top, with the hardest stretches last.
sides.highlights: San Romolo as a stop halfway up, and the view over Sanremo and the coast at the top.

monte-bisbino.intro: The home climb of Como's cyclists: from Cernobbio on the lake through forest to the pilgrimage church on the summit. At the top the view reaches over the southern part of Lake Como to the Po plain.

sides.character: From Cernobbio evenly steep in a long chain of hairpins through forest, hardly any traffic. A climb for finding your rhythm.
sides.highlights: The church on the summit and the view over Lake Como.

monte-bondone.intro: Trento's home mountain and a Giro climb since 1956, the year Charly Gaul won here in a snowstorm. From the Adige it climbs over 1,400 metres in one go, through dozens of hairpins.

sides.character: From Trento off the valley floor, hairpin after hairpin, getting steeper towards the top. Long and hard, the classic Giro ascent with the city and the Adige valley below you.
sides.highlights: Views down onto Trento and the Adige valley.

sides.character: From Sardagna, already well above Trento, steadily steep through many hairpins. Shorter than the main ascent, but without any flat stretches.

monte-ceneri.intro: The low saddle between Sopraceneri and Sottoceneri in Ticino, the road link between Bellinzona, Locarno and Lugano. Less busy since the Ceneri base tunnel, but no quiet road.

sides.character: From Cadenazzo on the Magadino plain steadily up through forest, a few wide bends on a broad road. The actual climb of the crossing.
From Rivera little more than a ramp: short and gentle up to the pass. The direction in which the crossing from Lugano happens almost in passing.

monte-generoso-bellavista.intro: A quiet dead end up Monte Generoso above Lake Lugano, as far as the Bellavista station of the rack railway. The summit above is left to the train and the walkers.

sides.character: Steeply up from Rovio through forest, alternating ramps and flatter sections, with a stretch of downhill on the way. The lake stays at your back.
sides.highlights: The view of Lake Lugano at Bellavista.

monte-pizzoc.intro: A short detour off the Cansiglio to the summit of Monte Pizzoc, on the southern edge of the plateau. At the top the view opens across the Venetian plain, on clear days as far as the lagoon.

sides.character: From the junction on the Cansiglio moderate at first, then increasingly steep to the summit. Short and easy to take in.
sides.highlights: From the summit, the view over the Venetian plain.

monte-san-primo.intro: The extension of the Ghisallo: from Bellagio past the chapel of the Madonna del Ghisallo and on via Magreglio to beneath Monte San Primo, the highest summit of the Larian Triangle. Views of Lake Como again and again on the way.

sides.character: From Bellagio up the Ghisallo road in hairpins, a flatter stretch after the chapel, then steeper again to the end of the tarmac. A long climb in stages.
sides.highlights: The Madonna del Ghisallo with its cycling museum.

monte-velo.intro: From Arco up to the alpine pastures above the Sarca valley, where the tarmac ends at the meadows of Monte Velo. Lake Garda lies far below to the south, the climbers' rock faces opposite.

sides.character: From Arco up the slope in many hairpins, growing steeper towards the top. The view over the Sarca valley widens with each bend.
sides.highlights: The view of Arco with its castle and Lake Garda.

monte-zoncolan.intro: Since 2003 the Giro has kept coming back to the Zoncolan, and the side from Ovaro counts among the steepest climbs in professional cycling. The scenery is humbler than the reputation: forest, then pastures and ski runs at the top.

sides.character: A wall: narrow and irregularly steep through forest from Ovaro, hardly a let-up, with short tunnels near the top. One to ride up only.
sides.highlights: At the top the arena of the Giro finishes.

sides.character: The milder side from Sutrio via the ski area, with flatter stretches and hairpins; it only gets really steep near the end. The better way down.

monte-zugna.intro: A detour on the edge of Rovereto up Monte Zugna, a front-line mountain between Italy and Austria-Hungary in the First World War. A long, quiet hairpin road to over 1,600 m.

sides.character: From Albaredo evenly steep in a long run of hairpins, through forest and higher up across open slopes looking into the Adige valley.
sides.highlights: First World War trenches and positions at the top.

moosalp.intro: A quiet crossing between two Valais valleys, without through traffic and with one of the widest views in the Upper Valais. Two sides that join into a loop from Visp.

sides.character: From Stalden steeply in hairpins to Törbel, then through forest and alpine pasture without a break to the top; the steeper side.
sides.highlights: The village of Törbel on its steep slope and the view into the Saas and Matter valleys.

sides.character: From Raron in hairpins to Unterbäch and on via Bürchen, more even and longer, at the top across open pasture.
sides.highlights: The view across the Rhône valley to the Bietschhorn and the Bernese Alps.

mottarone.intro: The viewpoint mountain between Lake Maggiore and Lake Orta, with both lakes at the top and the Valais Alps with Monte Rosa beyond. From Stresa a private toll road leads up; the climb from Armeno is a public road without a toll.

sides.character: From Armeno via Gignese, with changing gradient, steep ramps and short recoveries, open pasture at the top.
sides.highlights: At the top the view of two lakes and Monte Rosa.

muro-di-sormano.intro: The Wall of Sormano is one of the steepest ramps ever used in a professional race. It disappeared from the Giro di Lombardia after 1962 and has been back since 2012; the gradients are painted on the tarmac.

sides.character: The measured line follows the regular road from Sormano to the Colma, even and moderately steep. The Wall itself is a short, far steeper section beside it.
sides.highlights: At the Colma the view over the Vallassina.

nassfeldpass.intro: A ski resort on the border between Carinthia and Friuli, with a northern ramp counted among the hardest in Austria. From the south the road winds up out of the Val Canale in long series of hairpins.

sides.character: From Tröpolach out of the Gail valley hard and without a break, through many hairpins and if anything steeper towards the top. The side you set out to climb.
From Pontebba evenly through a long series of hairpins, hardly any outliers in the gradient. Just as demanding but more predictable, and good in either direction.

nevegal.intro: A short climb above Belluno, good for half a day.

sides.character: From Belluno gently through Castion, then steadily through forest and across meadows to the resort.
sides.highlights: The view across the Piave valley to the Belluno Dolomites.

nigerpass.intro: The quiet side door to the Rosengarten: while through traffic takes the Karerpass, this road climbs steeply and in shade up from Tiers. At the top the wall stands right above you.

sides.character: From Tiers through forest, getting steeper towards the top, with a number of hairpins. Only just below the top do the trees fall back and reveal the Rosengarten wall.
sides.highlights: The Rosengarten wall directly above the top of the pass.

nockalmstrasse.intro: A panoramic road through the rounded summits of the Nock mountains in the biosphere park, with two high points: the Eisentalhöhe and the Schiestelscharte. More rollers than a pass, with many hairpins and wide pastures.

sides.character: From Innerkrems a short way to the Eisentalhöhe, stepped with flat stretches and a few hairpins over pastures.
From Ebene Reichenau the whole road: over the Schiestelscharte, a lot of height back down into the valley and up again to the Eisentalhöhe, with many hairpins. The side to ride uphill as a tour.

norbertshoehe.intro: A hairpin road from the Lower Engadine up to the Nauders plateau which, with the Finstermünz gorge closed to bikes, has become the real cycle route to the Reschenpass. The Via Claudia Augusta runs on it too.

sides.character: From Martina straight into a series of hairpins on the slope above the Inn, even and without hard ramps to the top. Rides well, but with buses and diverted traffic.
sides.highlights: The view down into the Lower Engadine and the Inn gorge.

nufenenpass.intro: The highest road pass lying entirely in Switzerland links the Goms with Ticino. Opened only in 1969, it is quieter than its neighbours the Furka and the Gotthard.

sides.character: From Ulrichen steadily steep up the Ägene valley, steeper still over bare slopes near the top. The hard side, better as a climb.
sides.highlights: The Gries reservoir with its wind turbines just before the top.

sides.character: From Airolo long and stepped up the Val Bedretto, flat at first, then in hairpins. A long, quiet descent.
sides.highlights: The quiet Val Bedretto.

oberalppass.intro: The Oberalp links Andermatt with the Surselva, with the railway carrying the Glacier Express beside the road. The lighthouse at the top recalls the nearby source of the Rhine in Lake Toma.

sides.character: From Andermatt first the wall of hairpins above the village, visible from below, then flatter across the upland to the top.
sides.highlights: The view back down to Andermatt from the hairpins.

sides.character: Long and stepped from Disentis through the Surselva villages via Sedrun, rarely steep. Wide and flowing on the way down.
sides.highlights: Disentis monastery at the start.

oberjoch.intro: With its 106 bends, the Jochstraße from Bad Hindelang is considered Germany's twistiest road. It is the main link into the Tannheimer Tal and correspondingly busy, but pleasantly even for cyclists.

sides.character: From Bad Hindelang straight into the bends of the Jochstraße, steepest low down, then flatter up to Oberjoch. Moderate, but rarely alone on the road.
sides.highlights: Looking back into the Ostrach valley.

oetztaler-gletscherstrasse.intro: Austria's highest tarmac road climbs from Sölden to the Rettenbach and Tiefenbach glaciers. Every autumn the Alpine Ski World Cup opens its season on the Rettenbach glacier. A climb almost entirely above the treeline, with little respite in the gradient.

sides.character: From Sölden past the toll booth and then long in double figures into the glacier valley, uneven with ramps. At the top nothing but rock, ice and ski lifts.
sides.highlights: Views back over the Ötztal and onto the glaciers of the Ötztal Alps

ofenpass.intro: The Ofenpass crosses the Swiss National Park with its mountain pine forests and leads into the Val Müstair, home of St John's Abbey, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

sides.character: Long and without hairpins from Zernez through the National Park's forest, in steps with short descents along the way. A long, flowing run downhill.
sides.highlights: A break at the Hotel Il Fuorn in the middle of the park.

sides.character: Shorter and steeper from Santa Maria, stepped, with a few hairpins up the slopes of the Val Müstair.
sides.highlights: The abbey at Müstair a few kilometres from the start.

orcieres-merlette.intro: A quiet ski resort in the Champsaur with a big Tour history: in 1971 Luis Ocaña rode away from Eddy Merckx here by almost nine minutes, and in 2020 Primož Roglič won the stage.

sides.character: From Pont-du-Fossé steady and moderate, stepped with hairpins above the Drac valley, up to the resort.

pass-thurn.intro: The crossing from the Kitzbühel Alps into the Salzach valley, with the Großvenediger opposite.

sides.character: From Mittersill in long hairpins on the south slope, steady and with a view of the Tauern.
sides.highlights: The view across the Pinzgau to the Großvenediger.

sides.character: From Jochberg flat and straight up the valley.
sides.highlights: The grassy mountains of the Kitzbühel Alps.

passo-brocon.intro: Between Valsugana and Primiero lies a pass without an audience: wide meadows, hardly any cars and the Pale di San Martino to the north. If you are after quiet rather than names, this is the place.

sides.character: From Castello Tesino long and in steps, with flatter sections and some hairpins in the upper part. Rarely steep, much forest and open meadows.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Pale di San Martino to the north.

passo-campolongo.intro: The lowest and gentlest pass of the Sellaronda, between Corvara and Arabba. In the Maratona dles Dolomites it is the first climb.

sides.character: From Arabba short and steeper at first, with a few hairpins, flattening towards the top. A quick hop over the saddle.
From Corvara steady and moderate through meadows and forest, with a few hairpins. The Maratona direction; pleasant both up and down.

passo-cereda.intro: A short crossing beneath the south faces of the Pale di San Martino, between Primiero and Agordo. Usually ridden as a link between bigger passes; the west side is short and full of hairpins, the east side long and gentle.

sides.character: Up from Fiera di Primiero in many hairpins, getting steeper towards the top. Compact and easy to pace, the rewarding side to climb.
sides.highlights: The south faces of the Pale above the Primiero.

sides.character: From Agordo long and in steps, with an intermediate saddle and a descent on the way, mostly gentle. Downhill a long, calm roll-out towards the Cordevole.

passo-cibiana.intro: A quiet crossing between the Cadore and the Zoldo valley, hardly any traffic and plenty of forest. The village of Cibiana is known for the murals on its houses; above the pass, on Monte Rite, stands one of Reinhold Messner's mountain museums.

sides.character: Up from the Piave valley at Valle di Cadore in steps, with flatter sections and a short descent on the way, hairpins in the forest higher up. Long, but nowhere steep for long.
sides.highlights: The painted house fronts of Cibiana di Cadore along the way.

passo-cimabanche.intro: Hardly a climb, more a long valley between the Pustertal and the Ampezzo, but one with a Dolomite backdrop. Usually ridden as the approach to the Drei Zinnen, Misurina or Cortina, with the old Dolomite railway as a cycle path alongside.

sides.character: From Toblach long and barely rising through the Höhlensteintal, past two lakes and with short flat stretches. Uphill, Monte Cristallo grows ahead of you.
sides.highlights: The Dürrensee with Monte Cristallo behind it.

sides.character: From Cortina just as gentle up through the forest along the Boite, with a bare plateau at the top. Downhill fast and open into the Cortina basin.
sides.highlights: The Tofane above the Ampezzo.

passo-croce-d-aune.intro: A low forest pass above Feltre that owes its fame to a story: this is where Tullio Campagnolo is said to have had the idea for the quick release. Today a quiet climb with a small village, hotels and inns at the top.

sides.character: From Pedavena steep and even at once in hairpins through the forest, with no flat stretches to the saddle. The side for climbing.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Campagnolo monument on the saddle.

sides.character: From Gorna more varied through the hamlets of Sovramonte, with flatter stretches and short dips between the hairpins. Downhill the finer side, with views over the valley.
sides.highlights: The villages of Sovramonte on the slope.

passo-crocedomini.intro: A lonely high road in the Brescia Alps between the Val Camonica and the Val Caffaro. High pastures and hardly any cars at the top, but a surface that is coarse in many places.

sides.character: From Breno the hard side: around 8 % throughout, uneven, with many hairpins through forest up to the pastures. Steep and twisting, better uphill.
From Bagolino up the Val Caffaro, gentler on average, alternating between ramps and calmer stretches, with many hairpins. The milder descent.

passo-d-ampola.intro: Not a mountain but the end of the Ledro valley: from the Lago di Ledro almost flat to the pass, then down to Storo in the Chiese valley. The road up the Tremalzo branches off here.

sides.character: From Molina along Lake Ledro and up the valley, hardly any gradient and no hairpins. Downhill, a roll back to the lake.
sides.highlights: The pile-dwelling museum at Molina on the lakeshore.

sides.character: From Storo in the Chiese valley the actual climb: hairpins and steep stretches, with a short downhill on the way. Up, the side with bite.

passo-d-eira.intro: The smaller of the two passes between Livigno and the Valtellina, right before the Foscagno. Short, usually taken in passing and busy because of duty-free Livigno.

sides.character: Out of the Livigno valley floor, short and moderately steep, a little steeper towards the top, with a few hairpins and a view over the high valley.
sides.highlights: The view back over Livigno and its lake.

passo-del-ballino.intro: The classic way from Lake Garda into the Trentino: from Riva via Tenno past the Lago di Tenno up onto the Fiavè plateau. Open all year and busy at weekends.

sides.character: From Riva steepest at the bottom in hairpins above the lake, calmer and gentler at the top. Downhill you ride towards Lake Garda, the finer direction.
sides.highlights: The turquoise Lago di Tenno and the village of Canale di Tenno.

sides.character: From Ponte Arche in the Giudicarie gently and in steps across the plateau, almost without hairpins. Up, the easy side.

passo-del-cason-di-lanza.intro: A lonely pass in the Carnic Alps, within reach of the Zoncolan.

sides.character: From Paularo narrow and steadily steep through forest and across pastures to the top.
sides.highlights: The pastures below the Zermula.

passo-del-faiallo.intro: From the sea at Genoa-Voltri past the Acquasanta sanctuary onto the crest of the Ligurian Alps. At the top the coast lies far below in the haze, the Po plain on the other side.

sides.character: From Voltri, practically at sea level, long and stepped, with steep ramps, flatter stretches and a short dip on the way. On the crest the view back to the sea.
sides.highlights: At the top the view over Genoa and its gulf.

passo-del-foscagno.intro: Anyone heading from Bormio into duty-free Livigno has to cross the Foscagno; the customs post still stands at the top. From Livigno you first cross the Passo d'Eira, then drop briefly to Trepalle.

sides.character: Stepped from Isolaccia with flatter stretches and few hairpins up the Valdidentro, on a wide road.
From Livigno first over the Passo d'Eira, then briefly down to Trepalle and up again. Mild, but with a counter-climb in either direction.

passo-del-ginestro.intro: The quiet neighbour of the Colle San Bartolomeo, open all year. Up through olives and broom, a view of both valleys at the top, and on the far side down to Cesio in the Arroscia valley.

sides.character: Long and irregular from Chiusanico through olives and broom, with flat stretches, a short dip and the odd steep ramp. The calmer choice downhill.
From Cesio only a short but steep pitch throughout, without hairpins. Quickly pushed up, a steep straight going down.

passo-del-maniva.intro: The Maniva lies between the Val Trompia and the Valle del Caffaro, with a ridge road joining at the top. Long climbs, very little traffic and on clear days a view as far as Lake Garda.

sides.character: From Bagolino in many hairpins through the forest, getting steeper towards the top. Long, steady work without a real break.
sides.highlights: At the top, on clear days, the view as far as Lake Garda.

passo-del-mortirolo.intro: On the Giro since 1990 and the byword for steepness; Marco Pantani's attack in 1994 made it a legend. No views, hardly any traffic, just forest and ramps.

sides.character: From Mazzo very steep from the start through forest and many hairpins, with no respite, a little easier only in the upper part. Only sensible as a climb.
sides.highlights: The Pantani memorial on the way up.

sides.character: From Monno much more moderate, with intermediate descents and short steep pitches. The side for the descent.

passo-del-redebus.intro: A quiet pass east of Trento, as a loop with the Piné plateau.

sides.character: From Pergine through the Fersina valley via Sant'Orsola and Palù, steady and long.
sides.highlights: The Mòcheni villages in the Fersina valley.

sides.character: From Bedollo on the plateau short and moderate.
sides.highlights: The Piné plateau.

passo-del-tonale.intro: The Tonale links the Valcamonica with the Val di Sole; at the top are a ski resort and the memorial to the fallen of the First World War, when the front ran through here. Often just the link to the Gavia or the Mortirolo.

sides.character: From Vezza d'Oglio gentle along the valley to Ponte di Legno at first, then steeper in hairpins up to the pass.
No hairpins from Vermiglio, steepest low down and flatter higher up, on a wide road. Fast downhill, but with traffic.

passo-del-turchino.intro: Since its first edition in 1907, Milan–Sanremo has crossed the Apennines here and caught its first sight of the sea. A low, busy crossing with a short tunnel at the top – famous for the race, not for the road.

sides.character: From Voltri on the coast steadily and gently up the Leira valley, more main road than mountain road; a few wide bends, never a moment that hurts.
sides.highlights: The tunnel at the top and the view over the Riviera, which the pros see in the opposite direction in the race.

passo-del-vivione.intro: One of the quietest mountain roads in the Bergamasque Alps, narrow and largely without crash barriers. It links the Val di Scalve with the Val Camonica and belongs to the few who find it.

sides.character: Moderate from Schilpario at first, then steeper in many tight hairpins up past the tree line into open ground.

passo-dell-aprica.intro: The main link between the Valtellina and the Val Camonica, and busy accordingly. In the Giro often the approach to the Mortirolo and the Gavia; in 1994 Marco Pantani won the stage over the Stelvio and the Mortirolo at Aprica.

sides.character: Up from the Valtellina at Tresenda in steps, steeper ramps between calmer stretches and the valley below. The more demanding side and the better one to climb.
sides.highlights: The view over the Valtellina and its vineyards.

sides.character: Long and flat from Edolo along the valley, only short steeper pitches. Rather tedious uphill, quick and open as a descent to Edolo.

passo-della-mauria.intro: The gentle link from the Dolomites into Carnia.

sides.character: From Lorenzago steadily through forest to the top.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Marmarole.

sides.character: From Forni di Sopra gently through the upper Tagliamento valley.
sides.highlights: The Friulian Dolomites above Forni.

passo-della-presolana.intro: The pass below the Presolana, easy to combine with the Vivione and the Zambla in a loop.

sides.character: From Clusone steadily via Castione della Presolana and through forest to the top.
sides.highlights: The south face of the Presolana above the top.
