sides.character: From Dezzo short and steeper in hairpins up out of the gorge.
sides.highlights: The Via Mala gorge of Scalve below Dezzo.

passo-delle-erbe.intro: The Würzjoch links the Val Badia with the Eisack valley near Brixen and lies right beneath the Peitlerkofel in the Puez-Odle nature park. Little traffic, narrow roads and alpine meadows.

sides.character: From St. Martin in Thurn stepped, with hairpins and a short downhill stretch, open at the top below the Peitlerkofel. As a descent the shorter side.
From Brixen long and stepped via the hillside villages, alternating between ramps and flatter stretches. The long climb, with the Peitlerkofel ahead as the goal.
sides.highlights: The Peitlerkofel right above the top

passo-delle-fittanze.intro: From Ala in the Adige valley onto the crest of the Lessinia: a good 1,200 metres in one go, with long ramps around 10 % and hardly any traffic. At the top the landscape turns to karst and pasture; on the other side there is only the plateau.

sides.character: Out of the valley via Sega di Ala in many hairpins, the rhythm uneven: long steep ramps alternate with short easier stretches. Pasture and karst open up at the top.
sides.highlights: At the top the open karst country of the Lessinia after the long climb.

passo-dello-stelvio.intro: The 48 numbered hairpins from Prad are the defining image of an Alpine pass. The second-highest road pass in the Alps is often the Giro's Cima Coppi, with the Ortler right opposite.

sides.character: From Prad moderate along the valley to Trafoi, then the wall of hairpins grows steeper to the top. You see what is coming, and it is best ridden up.
sides.highlights: The view down the hairpin wall and across to the Ortler.

sides.character: From Bormio even through galleries and hairpins, past the Umbrail junction. Wider bends, the better side for the descent.
sides.highlights: The baths of Bormio at the foot of the climb.

passo-di-agueglio.intro: From Lake Como at Varenna up via Perledo and Esino Lario and down into the Valsassina. The lake side, with its hairpins and the view of Bellagio, is one of the finest climbs on the eastern shore.

sides.character: From Varenna up the lake flank in many hairpins, with flatter stretches in the villages. The lake and Bellagio lie behind and below you; downhill the tight bends are rather work.
sides.highlights: The view from Perledo across the lake to Bellagio.

sides.character: From Parlasco in the Valsassina short and even. Downhill, the quick way into the valley.

passo-di-campogrosso.intro: A steep, shady climb from Recoaro Terme to beneath the rock walls of the Little Dolomites, with a rifugio at the top. Only this side is tarmac, so you ride up here and back down the same way.

sides.character: From Recoaro up the slope in close hairpins, moderate lower down, steeper towards the top. Plenty of forest and shade, and at the end the walls of the Little Dolomites stand right above the road.
sides.highlights: The rock walls of the Little Dolomites above the summit, and the rifugio for a break.

passo-di-costalunga.intro: The Karerpass is the main road from the Eggental into the Val di Fassa and correspondingly busy. It is worth riding all the same: just below the top the Karersee and the Rosengarten wall lie along the way.

sides.character: From Welschnofen with a changing gradient and a few hairpins through forest, past the Karersee, with the Latemar and the Rosengarten in view. The more varied side, better ridden upwards.
sides.highlights: The Karersee with the Latemar behind it, just below the top.

sides.character: From Vigo di Fassa gentle and in steps on a wide road with hardly any hairpins. More a feeder going up, but a flowing descent into the Val di Fassa.

passo-di-gavia.intro: The snowstorm stage of the 1988 Giro, which put Andy Hampsten on course for overall victory, made the Gavia famous. Narrow, high and wild, with the Lago Bianco at the top.

sides.character: From Ponte di Legno narrow and ever steeper, with an unlit tunnel in the upper part. Superb going up, tricky going down.
sides.highlights: The Lago Bianco just before the top.

sides.character: From Bormio via Santa Caterina Valfurva, long and stepped with flatter sections, open pasture near the top. The more readable side for the descent.

passo-di-valcava.intro: One of the steepest climbs in northern Italy: from Torre de' Busi over 1,000 metres in one go, a wall of hairpins above the Val San Martino. The east side from the Valle Imagna is the tamed half.

sides.character: From Torre de' Busi hard from the start and steeper still towards the top, hairpin after hairpin without a rest. Up, a test; down, nothing but braking.
From the Valle Imagna steady and much tamer, through forest and meadows. The side to descend.

passo-duran.intro: A quiet crossing between Agordo and the Zoldo valley, squeezed between the Moiazza and the San Sebastiano. Hardly any traffic, narrow, and with long, steep straights on the Agordo side.

sides.character: From Agordo steadily steep, almost without hairpins, through forest and past hamlets. Long steep straights, better ridden uphill.
From Forno di Zoldo stepped and more moderate, with a few hairpins and a short downhill stretch. The friendlier descent.

passo-falzarego.intro: The front line of the First World War ran between Cortina and Livinallongo; at the top the tunnels in the Lagazuoi recall it. The Falzarego is part of the Maratona dles Dolomites and a busy crossing all year round.

sides.character: From Cortina in wide hairpins through forest and then open ground below the Tofane and the Cinque Torri. Wide and clear; as a descent with views over the Ampezzo basin.
From Caprile long and stepped up into the Livinallongo, past Andraz castle and in many hairpins to the top. The longer side, better uphill.

passo-fedaia.intro: At the top the road runs along a reservoir beneath the Marmolada glacier, the largest in the Dolomites. The east side, with its long straight from Malga Ciapela, is among the hardest ramps around; in 2022 the Giro was decided here.

sides.character: Easy for a long time from Caprile, then from Malga Ciapela it suddenly turns steep: an almost straight ramp with few hairpins up to the reservoir. A test uphill, hard braking downhill.
sides.highlights: The Marmolada appears at the end of the straight.

sides.character: The gentlest way up, from Canazei: moderate through forest, a little steeper towards the end, then flat along the lake shore. Flowing on the way down.
sides.highlights: At the top the reservoir below the Marmolada's north face.

passo-furcia.intro: The shortest way from the Pustertal into the Val Badia region: Olang on one side, St. Vigil in Enneberg on the other. An honest climb in the shadow of the Kronplatz, far less busy than the big Dolomite passes.

sides.character: From Olang through forest and a handful of hairpins, getting steeper towards the top. Little view on the way; at the top the meadows below the Kronplatz open up.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Kronplatz directly above the road.

passo-gardena.intro: The Gardena pass links Val Gardena with the Val Badia and is one of the four Sellaronda passes. At the top the Sella towers rise on one side, the Cir peaks on the other.

sides.character: From Corvara via Colfosco at a steady 6 % in a run of hairpins below the Sassongher. A rhythm that carries you uphill.
From Wolkenstein stepped and gentler, with hairpins and short breathers, open at the top below the Cir peaks. As a descent with views of the Sella.

passo-giau.intro: For many the most beautiful pass in the Dolomites, with Ra Gusela and the Nuvolau almost within reach at the top. The steep south side is part of the Maratona dles Dolomites, and in 2021 the Giau was the Giro's Cima Coppi.

sides.character: The hard side: steep and irregular through forest from Selva di Cadore, then in tight hairpins over alpine meadows to the top. One to climb rather than descend.
sides.highlights: Ra Gusela and the Nuvolau rise up ahead of your front wheel.

sides.character: Longer and milder from Cortina, in steps via Pocol with flatter stretches between. Wide views of the Tofane make it the nicer way down.
sides.highlights: The Tofane above the Cortina basin.

passo-lavaze.intro: A pass of meadow rather than rock: at the top lies a wide plateau between Latemar and Schwarzhorn, cross-country skiing country in winter. The south side out of the Val di Fiemme is short and steep, the north side via Deutschnofen long and rolling.

sides.character: From Cavalese straight up the slope without hairpins, steep throughout and irregular, with sections well above the average. A test uphill, straight and fast downhill.
From Deutschnofen through meadows and forest in steps, with flat stretches and short descents on the way. Little gradient, plenty of landscape; the more pleasant side to descend.
sides.highlights: Latemar and Rosengarten in view above the meadows.

passo-manghen.intro: The Manghen crosses the lonely Lagorai range between the Valsugana and the Fiemme valley. Narrow, steep and nearly free of traffic, and with over 1600 metres from the Valsugana one of the hardest climbs in Trentino.

sides.character: From Borgo Valsugana long and ever steeper towards the top, through forest and finally in hairpins over open slopes. The hard side, to be ridden uphill.
From Molina di Fiemme through the Val Cadino, stepped and more moderate, with a stretch that gives height back. The milder descent.

passo-monte-croce-comelico.intro: The Kreuzberg pass links the Sexten valley with the Comelico; in the First World War the front ran here. A gentle crossing with the Sexten Dolomites in view.

sides.character: From Innichen via Sexten flat and stepped, hardly any hairpins, the Sexten Dolomites in front of you. A calm roll both up and down.
sides.highlights: The Sexten Dolomites above the Fischleintal

sides.character: From Padola short, with ups and downs and a few hairpins through forest to the saddle.

passo-pampeago.intro: The Reiterjoch below the Latemar links the Val di Fiemme with the Eggental and is known above all as the Giro summit finish at the Alpe di Pampeago. For the 2012 Giro the last stretch to the pass was paved, and since then it is a through road that stays closed to cars.

sides.character: From Tesero steep at once and hardly easing up through the forest to the ski station, then steeper again on the car-free stretch to the pass. Hard and even; downhill it is the wider road.
sides.highlights: On the way, the memorial to the Stava disaster of 1985.

sides.character: From Birchabruck with very steep ramps up to Obereggen, then single-track and quieter through forest and across pastures to the pass. Uncomfortable downhill because of the ramps and the narrow road.
sides.highlights: The Latemar above the pastures near Obereggen.

passo-pordoi.intro: One of the four Sellaronda passes and one of the most-raced climbs of the Giro d'Italia. At the top a memorial recalls Fausto Coppi, with the Marmolada opposite.

sides.character: Short and even: from Arabba a ladder of hairpins climbs the open meadows of the east flank, with the next bends always in view ahead.
sides.highlights: At the top the Marmolada and its glacier straight across.

sides.character: The longer west side climbs evenly from Canazei through forest, then in many hairpins below the walls of the Sella massif.
sides.highlights: The rock walls of the Sella massif right above the road.

passo-rest.intro: A quiet pass in the Carnian backcountry, for days without traffic.

sides.character: From Tramonti di Sopra steadily through forest.
sides.highlights: The green Tramonti valleys.

sides.character: From Socchieve long and moderate via the villages on the Tagliamento slope.
sides.highlights: The view over the Tagliamento valley.

passo-rolle.intro: The Rolle passes beneath the Pale di San Martino, with the Cimon della Pala, the Matterhorn of the Dolomites, above the top. On the north side lies the Paneveggio forest, whose spruce violin makers prize as tonewood.

sides.character: From Predazzo long and stepped through the Paneveggio forest, with flatter stretches and hairpins only in the upper part. As a descent long and flowing.
From Fiera di Primiero via San Martino di Castrozza steady and long, with many hairpins and the Pale in front of you. The finer way up.
sides.highlights: The Pale di San Martino above San Martino di Castrozza

passo-san-bernardino.intro: Since the motorway tunnel took the traffic, the old pass road between the Misox and the Rheinwald has been quiet. At the top lies Lake Moesola among rocky knolls.

sides.character: Long and stepped from Mesocco, with a great many hairpins and flatter stretches via the village of San Bernardino. A climb with rhythm.
sides.highlights: The castle ruin of Mesocco at the start.

sides.character: Shorter and mild from Hinterrhein, stepped with a small dip on the way, the hairpins wide over open ground.
sides.highlights: Lake Moesola at the top.

passo-san-boldo.intro: A road you ride for the way it was built: hairpin after hairpin lies in tunnels in the rock, stacked one above the other in the wall above Tovena. Low, short and unique in the southern Alps.

sides.character: From Tovena unremarkable at first, then the wall with the hairpin tunnels, tight and controlled by lights, often with a short wait. Irregular, with short steep bits in the tunnels.
sides.highlights: The view from below of the stacked tunnel hairpins in the rock face.

passo-san-marco.intro: The road follows the old Via Priula, which Venice had built from Bergamo to the Valtellina in the late 16th century. Today it is a quiet link between the Val Brembana and the Valtellina, and with some 1700 metres from Morbegno one of the longest climbs in the area.

sides.character: Out of the Valtellina through the Bitto valley: long and uneven, flatter stretches between steep ramps and a run of hairpins higher up. The big climb, better ridden uphill.
Out of the Val Brembana shorter, moderate low down, steeper higher up with hairpins over open slopes. As a descent the clearer choice.
sides.highlights: Ca' San Marco, the old inn on the Via Priula just below the top

passo-san-pellegrino.intro: The San Pellegrino links the Fassa valley at Moena with the Biois valley and Falcade. At the top a broad saddle with a ski area; the east side is clearly the steeper one.

sides.character: From Moena steeper at first through forest, then easing, almost without hairpins to the broad top. As a descent straight and fast.
From Falcade steadily steep in a run of hairpins, with steeper ramps. The side for climbing.

passo-sant-antonio.intro: A quiet forest pass between the Ansiei valley at Auronzo and the Comelico, also called Passo del Zovo. Short, but steep throughout on the south side, and with Monte Croce Comelico a loop around the Comelico.

sides.character: Flat out of Auronzo, then steep in the middle section with hairpins through the forest; the view opens near the top. A side for climbing, uncomfortable downhill because of the ramps.
sides.highlights: At the top, the view across the forests of the Comelico.

sides.character: From Padola short with a few steep pitches, on a wide road with a good surface. Downhill the pleasanter side into the Comelico.
sides.highlights: Padola below the meadows of the Comelico.

passo-santa-barbara.intro: The crossing from Rovereto into the Val di Gresta above the northern end of Lake Garda, crossed by the Giro d'Italia in 2025. Two very different sides: long and stepped from the Adige valley, short and steep from Nago.

sides.character: From Rovereto a long way via Isera and in many hairpins, with rests and a stretch of downhill on the way. Flowing enough for the descent into the Adige valley.
From Nago via Ronzo, very steep at the bottom, easing towards the top. A climb you would rather ride up than down.
sides.highlights: The view back to Lake Garda above Nago.

passo-sella.intro: The Sella sits between Val di Fassa and Val Gardena right beneath the Sella towers, with the Sassolungo next door. As part of the Sellaronda it is busy in summer.

sides.character: From Canazei on the Pordoi road at first, then the road branches off and climbs in steps, with a short drop on the way, in hairpins below the Sella towers.
sides.highlights: The Sella towers right above the last hairpins.

sides.character: Calmer from Wolkenstein, with flatter stretches via Plan de Gralba and few hairpins. Downhill you roll into Val Gardena with the Sassolungo in view.
sides.highlights: The Sassolungo beside the road.

passo-sommo.intro: The way out of the Adige valley onto the Folgaria plateau: the real work is the hairpin road up from Calliano, the pass beyond it is little more than a rise. Almost 1,200 metres straight above the valley, a serious climb without a big name.

sides.character: From Calliano up the valley side in hairpins, looking back into the Adige valley; a real climb as far as Folgaria, then rolling with short respites to the top.
sides.highlights: The view back into the Adige valley from the hairpins below Folgaria.

passo-staulanza.intro: The Staulanza links the Zoldo valley with Selva di Cadore and runs right along the west flank of the Pelmo. Quieter than the big Dolomite passes and open all year.

sides.character: From Forno di Zoldo long and stepped along the valley and then up in hairpins, briefly with a downhill stretch, the Pelmo in front of you.
sides.highlights: The Pelmo up close

sides.character: From Selva di Cadore short and moderate, with few hairpins through forest and meadows. As a descent short and clear.

passo-teglia.intro: One of the highest tarmac crossings in the Sanremo hinterland, almost 1,400 m up, links the Argentina valley with Rezzo. From chestnut forest up to the open pasture on the ridge, with almost nobody in between.

sides.character: Straight up from Molini di Triora, evenly steep through chestnut forest, hairpin after hairpin. No flat bit to recover on, but a clear rhythm.
From Rezzo gently at first, then steadily steeper, with the hard parts higher up. The longer, more flowing side, good for descending towards Pieve di Teco.

passo-tre-croci.intro: The low saddle between Cristallo and Sorapiss links Cortina with Misurina. In the Giro d'Italia it has several times been the approach to the summit finish at the Tre Cime; on its own it is a short, friendly climb through forest.

sides.character: Out of Cortina evenly through larch forest, a few hairpins and a little steeper in the upper part. The pass's real ascent, and the nicer direction to ride it uphill.
sides.highlights: Looking back over Cortina and the Tofane, Cristallo and Sorapiss on either side at the top.

sides.character: From Misurina more a rolling link than a climb: briefly downhill, then gently back up to the top. As the way down towards Misurina it holds no difficulties.
sides.highlights: Shortly before Misurina, the view to the Cadini di Misurina.

passo-tremalzo.intro: A detour from the Val di Ledro to over 1,700 m, with the tarmac ending at the pass. Beyond it starts the famous gravel road with tunnels towards Lake Garda, a mountain-bike classic.

sides.character: From the junction in the Ledro valley evenly steep through forest and in many hairpins, more open at the top with views of the mountains around Lake Ledro.

passo-valles.intro: The Valles links the Biois valley with the Travignolo valley and is usually ridden in a loop with the Rolle and San Pellegrino. Narrow and little used, with the Paneveggio forest on the west side and open pastures at the top.

sides.character: From Falcade long and steadily steep, with a few hairpins and the final kilometres above the tree line. The harder side, and one that rewards a good rhythm.
sides.highlights: The open pastures above the tree line before the top.

sides.character: From Paneveggio short, with barely a hairpin, through the forest at first and then steeper to the top. Downhill the calmer line back towards the Rolle.
sides.highlights: The spruce forest of Paneveggio, famous for its tonewood.

passo-valparola.intro: The Valparola lies only a little over a kilometre of road from the Falzarego and leads down into the Val Badia. At the top stands the Tre Sassi fort with a First World War museum, and a small lake below the Lagazuoi.

sides.character: From Stern via San Cassiano gently along the valley first, then stepped and steeper in hairpins over open pastures to the top.
sides.highlights: The Tre Sassi fort and the Valparola lake at the top

passo-vezzena.intro: The way from Lake Caldonazzo onto the plateau of Lavarone and Asiago, via the hairpins of the old Menador road, the Kaiserjägerstraße. The north side is the climb, the south side from the Asiago plateau barely one.

sides.character: From Caldonazzo in hairpins up the rock face onto the plateau, then on in steps across meadows and forest to the pass, with short counter-climbs.
sides.highlights: The view of Lake Caldonazzo from the hairpins.

sides.character: From the Asiago plateau gently and in steps across open pasture, hardly any hairpins. Downhill a calm roll back onto the plateau.

passo-xomo.intro: The little neighbour of the Fugazze above Valli del Pasubio, short and steep. From here the Strada degli Scarubbi continues as a gravel track towards the Pasubio.

sides.character: From Sant'Antonio up in steps and hairpins, with flatter sections between the ramps. Downhill the clearer side.
From Posina quiet and short, steeper and steeper towards the top. The climb with bite, better ridden up.

passwang.intro: A moderate pass in the Solothurn Jura, close to Basel.

sides.character: From Mümliswil steadily in hairpins to the tunnel.
sides.highlights: The Jura heights above the Thal.

sides.character: From Beinwil steadily up the Lüssel valley.
sides.highlights: The quiet Lüssel valley.

pavlicevo-sedlo.intro: The quieter neighbour of the Seeberg saddle, with a view into the Kamnik–Savinja Alps.

sides.character: From Solčava through forest and past mountain farms steadily to the border.
sides.highlights: The Kamnik–Savinja Alps above the Logar valley.

sides.character: From Bad Eisenkappel long through the Vellach valley, at the top over a rise to the border.
sides.highlights: The quiet Leppen valley.

penegal.intro: From the Mendel Pass almost 400 m further up to the lookout tower on the Penegal. Short, steep and with one of the widest views over the Adige valley.

sides.character: From the Mendel Pass straight away steep through forest and a tight series of hairpins, easing a little towards the top. A short, hard second helping.
sides.highlights: From the tower, the view over the Adige valley to the Dolomites.

penserjoch.intro: The crossing from the Sarntal into the Wipptal near Sterzing is the quieter alternative to the Jaufen. Wide pastures above the treeline at the top, and from the south a long, easy run-in through the whole Sarntal.

sides.character: From Sarnthein long and stepped, with plenty of flat valley and the steeper part only at the top over the pastures. As a descent long and flowing.
From Sterzing much steeper, stepped with ramps and short breathers, through forest and then open pastures. The better way up.

pfaender.intro: A short climb with a big view: Lake Constance below, the Swiss Alps opposite.

sides.character: Steep right out of Bregenz up the slope, via Fluh through forest and meadows to the top station.
sides.highlights: The view over Lake Constance as far as the Säntis.

pian-del-re.intro: To the end of the Po valley, with the Monviso as a wall above the finish.

sides.character: From Paesana gently up the valley to Crissolo, then narrow and steep in hairpins via Pian della Regina to the Pian del Re.
sides.highlights: The north face of the Monviso and the source of the Po.

pian-delle-fugazze.intro: The crossing from the Adige valley into the Val Leogra beneath the Pasubio, a front line in the First World War and already ridden by the Giro in 1934. Near the pass, the Pasubio ossuary stands on the Colle Bellavista.

sides.character: From Rovereto a long way through the Vallarsa, in steps with flat stretches and short counter-climbs, hairpins at the top. Downhill a long, quiet ride back to the Adige valley.
From Valli del Pasubio short and steep in hairpins, hardest at the top. The side for climbing.
sides.highlights: A detour just before the pass to the Ossario del Pasubio on the Colle Bellavista.

piani-dei-resinelli.intro: From Ballabio above Lecco in hairpins beneath the rock walls of the Grigna, until the road ends on the Resinelli plateau. Steep, shady and with a view of Lecco and the lake.

sides.character: From Ballabio straight into a tight run of hairpins, hardest at the bottom, a little easier towards the top. Mostly in shade.
sides.highlights: The walls of the Grigna and the view of Lecco.

pila.intro: Aosta's own mountain: 1,200 m of climbing straight out of the town to a ski station with a view of the four-thousanders on both sides of the valley.

sides.character: Across the Dora to Gressan and then in many hairpins through meadows and forest, with no flat section and no steep ramp.
sides.highlights: The view down onto Aosta and across to the Grand Combin.

piller-sattel.intro: A small pass between the Pitztal and the Inn valley that ties the Kaunertal, the Pitztal and Landeck into one loop. At the top moor and larches instead of rock.

sides.character: From Wenns at the mouth of the Pitztal steadily through forest and over meadows up to the plateau.
sides.highlights: The high moor at Piller and the view back into the Pitztal.

sides.character: From Fließ short and very steep in hairpins up the slope; to be taken carefully as a descent.
sides.highlights: The Gacher Blick, a viewing platform above the Inn valley.

pitztal-mittelberg.intro: The Pitztal leads deep into the Ötztal Alps up to beneath the Wildspitze, the highest mountain in Tyrol. A long valley ride with little gradient that only ends at the glacier car park in Mittelberg.

sides.character: Up the valley from Jerzens: long flat stretches through the villages, short steps in between. More of a ride out than a climb, with the glaciers at the valley head ahead.
sides.highlights: The glaciers beneath the Wildspitze at the valley head.

pla-d-adet.intro: The shorter Tour climb above Saint-Lary, the forerunner of the Portet.

sides.character: From Saint-Lary steeply via Soulan, then steadier to the resort.
sides.highlights: The view into the Aure valley.

plateau-de-beille.intro: One of the Tour's hardest summit finishes, without a flat metre.

sides.character: From Les Cabannes steadily at 8 % through forest, across open pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The view over the upper Ariège valley.

plateau-des-glieres.intro: On this plateau above the Thorens valley a Resistance maquis held out in 1944 until it was crushed; the memorial at the top recalls it. The Tour came up in 2018 and 2020, both times with a gravel stretch across the plateau.

sides.character: From Thorens-Glières in steps through forest and meadows, steep ramps alternating with short breathers, and even a brief descent on the way. At the top the plateau opens out all at once.
sides.highlights: The Resistance memorial at the edge of the open plateau.

ploeckenpass.intro: The Romans already crossed here from Carinthia to Carnia. In the First World War the front ran across the top of the pass; today an open-air museum of positions and trenches recalls it.

sides.character: From Kötschach-Mauthen through the Valentin valley in steps, with a short descent on the way and the hairpins in the upper part. Moderately steep and even enough to flow well downhill.
From Paluzza via Timau long and moderate, then markedly steeper with many hairpins in the final kilometres. The side to climb, with its climax at the end.
sides.highlights: At the top, the positions of the open-air museum at the pass.

plose.intro: The long climb above Brixen, as an opener for the Würzjoch loop or as a day of its own.

sides.character: From Brixen steadily via St. Andrä, then through forest and across pastures to Palmschoss and the Kreuztal.
sides.highlights: The Odle peaks and the Peitlerkofel opposite.

poggio-di-sanremo.intro: The last climb of Milan–Sanremo, where the race has been decided since 1960: a few kilometres between greenhouses, the village at the top, then the descent to the Via Roma. Low, gentle, and still one of the most famous hills in cycling.

sides.character: Gently up from the coast road at Bussana between greenhouses, with a few hairpins and a short steeper bit before the village. Anyone who wants to can sprint the crest as in the race.
sides.highlights: The village of Poggio at the top, the Via Roma waiting below.

pokljuka.intro: The home climb of Bled's cyclists, onto a quiet forest plateau.

sides.character: From Gorje steadily through spruce forest onto the plateau, flatter at the top.
sides.highlights: The Pokljuka pastures and the view of Triglav.

port-d-envalira.intro: The highest point of the Pyrenean roads, more altitude than beauty.

sides.character: From Canillo via Soldeu and Grau Roig steadily to the top.
sides.highlights: The height above 2,400 m.

sides.character: From L'Hospitalet through the upper Ariège valley to Pas de la Casa, then in hairpins to the top.
sides.highlights: The hairpins above Pas de la Casa.

port-de-bales.intro: The loneliest of the big Pyrenean passes.

sides.character: From Mauléon long and gentle through the Ourse valley, then steep and narrow across the pastures.
sides.highlights: The pastures below the top.

sides.character: From Luchon via the villages of the Oueil valley, narrow and irregular.
sides.highlights: The quiet Oueil valley.

port-de-la-bonaigua.intro: Catalonia's big pass, long and open.

sides.character: From Esterri long and steady, in wide hairpins across the pastures at the top.
sides.highlights: The hairpins of the east side.

sides.character: From Vielha through the upper Aran via Salardú and Baqueira, moderate.
sides.highlights: The villages of the upper Aran.

port-de-lers.intro: The Agnes's neighbour, with a mountain lake at the top.

sides.character: From Vicdessos steadily steep through forest.
sides.highlights: The view into the Vicdessos valley.

sides.character: From Massat long and gentle via Le Port.
sides.highlights: The Étang de Lers.

port-del-canto.intro: A long pass in the Catalan hinterland, between Sort and La Seu.

sides.character: From Sort steadily in hairpins up the slope.
sides.highlights: The view into the Noguera Pallaresa valley.

sides.character: From Adrall long and moderate through forest.
sides.highlights: The Alt Urgell forests.

postalm.intro: One of the largest alpine pastures in Austria, reached by a toll road from the Wolfgangsee. Not a summit in the strict sense but a wide, treeless plateau you roll across almost level before dropping into the Lammertal.

sides.character: From Strobl up through forest in hairpins onto the plateau, then a long, almost level stretch across the pastures and finally down in hairpins into the Lammertal.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Wolfgangsee, the open pasture at the top.

pra-loup.intro: This is where the Merckx era ended in 1975: Bernard Thévenet caught him on the climb to Pra-Loup and took the yellow jersey, which he wore to Paris. A short, even climb above Barcelonnette.

sides.character: From Barcelonnette even and moderate, stepped with a few hairpins through larch forest to the resort, with views back into the Ubaye valley.
sides.highlights: View across the Ubaye valley

praebichl.intro: The crossing at the Styrian Erzberg, whose mining terraces can be seen from the road. A loop with the Leopoldsteiner See.

sides.character: Out of Eisenerz steadily past the Erzberg through forest to the top.
sides.highlights: The Erzberg with its terraces.

sides.character: From Vordernberg short and somewhat steeper through forest.
sides.highlights: The old ironworks in Vordernberg.

pragelpass.intro: A narrow, steep mountain road between the Muotatal and the Klöntal, closed to cars on Sundays and public holidays. The Klöntalersee lies on the east side as the reward.

sides.character: Long and stepped from Muotathal, steep ramps alternating with short recovery stretches. Narrow, few hairpins, plenty of forest and pasture.

prato-nevoso.intro: A short, steep resort climb between Cuneo and Liguria.

sides.character: From Frabosa Sottana steadily at around 8 % through forest and hairpins to the resort.
sides.highlights: The view over the Mondovì plain.

predilpass.intro: The old border crossing between the Val Canale and the Soča valley, usually ridden as the opener to the Vršič. Two very different sides: gentle past the Raibler See in the north, steep down the Koritnica valley to Bovec in the south.

sides.character: Flat from Tarvisio to Cave del Predil, then along the lake and up in steps to the summit. Easy-going uphill, quick and open as a descent.
sides.highlights: The Raibler See just below the summit.

sides.character: Out of the Soča valley through the narrow Koritnica valley, irregular with short very steep ramps. Better climbed than descended, where the steep straights demand hard braking.
sides.highlights: The Kluže fortress above the Koritnica gorge.

punta-veleno.intro: The steepest climb on Lake Garda: from the shore at Brenzone up the flank of Monte Baldo, with ramps up to 20 %. At the top the road tips over towards Prada Alta.

sides.character: Steep from the lakeshore without a run-up and steeper still above, hardly any hairpins, the road heads straight up the slope. Bring your smallest gear.
sides.highlights: The view straight down onto Lake Garda.

radstaedter-tauernpass.intro: A long Tauern crossing with a ski resort at the top. Since the motorway goes through the tunnel there is room on the pass road.

sides.character: From Radstadt first flat through the Taurach valley, from Untertauern steep in hairpins past the Gnadenfall waterfall, flatter at the top.
sides.highlights: The Gnadenfall waterfall at the steep step.

sides.character: From Mauterndorf via Tweng steadily through the Taurach valley.
sides.highlights: Mauterndorf castle at the start.

reschenpass.intro: The old Via Claudia Augusta crossing from the Inn to the Adige, today a wide transit road. It is known above all for the church tower of old Graun rising out of the Reschensee, and for the open Malser Haide with the Ortler behind.

sides.character: From Mals the only noticeable climb is across the Malser Haide up to the Haidersee, then almost level along the two lakes. Often into a headwind and with heavy traffic; a cycle path runs alongside.
sides.highlights: The church tower in the Reschensee at Graun.

rhemes-notre-dame.intro: A detour at the entrance of the Valsavarenche into the Val di Rhêmes, the westernmost valley of the Gran Paradiso area. The road ends in Rhêmes-Notre-Dame before a wide valley head.

sides.character: From the junction near Introd up the valley in steps, steep ramps alternating with long flatter stretches through villages and meadows.

riale.intro: The northernmost valley of Piedmont, reaching north between the Valais and Ticino. The road ends above one of the highest waterfalls in the Alps, on a high plain with a reservoir.

sides.character: Long and flat through the Valle Antigorio, then in steps through the Walser villages of the Val Formazza; the steepest part is the hairpins beside the waterfall.
sides.highlights: The Cascata del Toce, at full flow on summer weekends.

riedbergpass.intro: Germany's highest pass road and one of its steepest too. It links the Iller valley at Obermaiselstein with Balderschwang and in summer is a short, hard test in the Allgäu.

sides.character: From Obermaiselstein straight up the slope without hairpins, irregular with steep sections in the upper part. Short, but hardly any chance to recover.
sides.highlights: At the top, the view across the Allgäu Alps.

rifugio-dei-forni.intro: A narrow dead end from Santa Caterina into the Valle dei Forni, up to the hut below the Forni glacier. Right in the Stelvio National Park.

sides.character: From Santa Caterina growing steeper through forest, with few hairpins, opening out at the top onto the glacier valley.
sides.highlights: The view of the Forni glacier.

risoul.intro: A Tour climb above Guillestre, quieter than the Vars and the Izoard next door.

sides.character: From Guillestre up the Vars road, then in steady hairpins through larch forest to the resort.
sides.highlights: The view across the Durance valley to the Pelvoux.

rittner-hochplateau.intro: The sun terrace above Bozen: first the hairpins out of the Adige valley, then almost level roads across meadows and larches, with the Rosengarten and the Schlern opposite. On top runs the Rittner Bahn, and near Lengmoos stand the earth pyramids.

sides.character: From Bozen first steeply out of the basin in hairpins, then in steps and finally almost level across the plateau towards Lengstein. Work below, a scenic cruise on top.
sides.highlights: The earth pyramids near Lengmoos and the view to the Rosengarten and Schlern.

rossfeld-panoramastrasse.intro: Germany's highest high road runs as a loop along the border with Austria. At the top a wide view over the Salzach valley and up to the Hoher Göll.

sides.character: From Berchtesgaden steep and stepped, with a short dip, then along the slope on the panoramic road at the top.
sides.highlights: The Hoher Göll and the view into the Salzach valley.

route-de-presles.intro: One of the bold cliff roads of the Vercors: it hangs above the walls of Choranche and slips through a handful of tunnels. At the top it ends in the village of Presles, with the Bourne far below.

sides.character: Up from Pont-en-Royans, moderate at first, then steeper as the road reaches the cliff and runs through the tunnels. The drop is beside you the whole way.
sides.highlights: The view down over the walls of Choranche into the Bourne valley.

route-des-cretes.intro: The crest road of the high Vosges, built as a supply road in the First World War. It runs over grassy domes with views of the Rhine plain and, on a clear day, the Alps; the Tour de France rides stretches of it too, such as from the Markstein to the Grand Ballon.

sides.character: From the Col de la Schlucht south over the Hohneck and the Markstein to the Grand Ballon: rolling with short climbs and descents, almost always open at crest height.
sides.highlights: The view over the Rhine plain, on clear days as far as the Alps.

saanenmoeser.intro: The link between the Simmental and Gstaad, more an approach than a pass, but part of every loop with the Jaunpass and the Col du Pillon.

sides.character: From Zweisimmen steadily across meadows on the slope.
sides.highlights: The high moor of Saanenmöser.

sides.character: From Saanen gently through Schönried.
sides.highlights: The view across the Saanenland.

saas-fee.intro: The road to the glacier village below the highest peaks of Switzerland. A long valley climb that only turns properly steep at the end.

sides.character: From Stalden along the Saaser Vispa with galleries and a moderate gradient to Saas-Grund, then steeply up in hairpins to the car park at the edge of the village.
sides.highlights: The Fee glacier hanging above the roofs of the village.

saint-veran.intro: A short detour to one of the highest villages in Europe, with timber houses and sundials. Easy to combine with a ride over the Agnello.

sides.character: From the junction near Molines moderately steep over open slopes, a little steeper towards the village. Short and easy, with wide views over the Queyras.
sides.highlights: The timber houses of Saint-Véran.

samnaun.intro: A remote Swiss high valley that is best reached across the border.

sides.character: From Vinadi through the gorge of the Schergenbach with tunnels, then steadily through the valley.
sides.highlights: The villages of the Samnaun valley below the Muttler.

santuario-di-oropa.intro: The sanctuary above Biella is one of the Giro's mountains in Piedmont, and tied to Marco Pantani. A climb of medium length that saves its steep part for the end.

sides.character: Out of the town first gently through suburbs and forest, the last kilometres steeper up to the square in front of the sanctuary.
sides.highlights: The baroque complex of the sanctuary at the end of the road.

santuario-di-sant-anna-di-vinadio.intro: The sanctuary at just over 2000 m is said to be the highest in Europe and sits at the end of a short spur above the Lombarde road. A Giro stage finished here in 2016.

sides.character: A short, steadily steep spur up from the pass road, with only two hairpins up to the sanctuary.
sides.highlights: The pilgrimage church at the end of the road.

sattelegg.intro: A quiet prealpine pass between the March district and the Sihlsee, an hour from Zurich.

sides.character: From Siebnen steadily via Vorderthal and up through forest.
sides.highlights: The view back across the Obersee.

sides.character: From Euthal on the Sihlsee short and moderate.
sides.highlights: The Sihlsee below the road.

sauris.intro: Gorge, reservoir and a language-island village: the finest detour in Carnia.

sides.character: From Ampezzo steadily into the Lumiei gorge, through several narrow tunnels to the dam, then along the lake and more steeply to Sauris di Sopra.
sides.highlights: The Lumiei gorge and the Lago di Sauris.

schallenberg.intro: A gentle hill pass between the Bernese Oberland and the Emmental, ideal for a loop with the Glaubenbielen.

sides.character: From Schwarzenegg gently across meadows to the top.
sides.highlights: The view back to the Niesen and the Stockhorn.

sides.character: From Marbach moderately through the Ilfis valley.
sides.highlights: The Emmental farms on the slopes.

schnalstal-kurzras.intro: From Naturns up to 2,000 m at the glacier, the whole valley a single dead end. Along the way lie the charterhouse of Karthaus and the Vernagt reservoir; the Iceman was found above the head of the valley in 1991.

sides.character: From Naturns steep at first through the narrow gorge, then irregular, flat stretches and fresh ramps all the way to Kurzras. Long, and the end drags.
sides.highlights: The Vernagt reservoir with the 3,000 m peaks behind it.

schoeckl.intro: The Graz town mountain with a view across all of eastern Styria, the after-work goal of the Graz road cyclists.

sides.character: Gently out of town to St. Radegund, then steeper and narrow in hairpins up to the Stubenberghaus.
sides.highlights: The all-round view from the summit plateau over Graz.

schwaegalp.intro: The summit lies right beneath the north face of the Säntis, and that wall carries the whole climb. The Säntis cable car starts at the top, with the Appenzell hill country all around.

sides.character: Up from Urnäsch through rolling country in steps, flat stretches between short steeper ones. For the last few kilometres the Säntis stands above the road.
sides.highlights: The north face of the Säntis over the last few kilometres.

seebergsattel.intro: A quiet border crossing between the Karawanks and the Kamnik Alps, east of the Loibl. Even, little used and more meadow than rock at the top, with the faces of Kočna and Grintovec above Jezersko.

sides.character: From Zgornje Jezersko moderate at first, then a little steeper through a few hairpins to the border. A short, quiet climb without surprises.
sides.highlights: Looking back to the Kamnik Alps above Jezersko.

seefelder-sattel.intro: The saddle between the Inn valley and the Seefeld plateau, one of the steepest federal roads in Austria. No pleasure climb, but the way north out of Innsbruck.

sides.character: Steep right out of Zirl on the slope, long straight ramps of up to 16 % with lorry traffic, flatter at the top up to Reith.
sides.highlights: The view across the Inn valley to Innsbruck and the Kalkkögel.

sides.character: From Scharnitz on the border only gently rising via Gießenbach to Seefeld.
sides.highlights: The Seefeld plateau with the Wetterstein range to the north.

seiser-alm.intro: Europe's largest high alpine pasture, with the Schlern and the Langkofel as a backdrop. Because the road is closed to cars during the day it belongs to cyclists and the service bus, one of the rare Dolomite climbs without sightseeing traffic.

sides.character: From Seis steadily and fairly steeply up through forest and hairpins, until the pasture opens out at Compatsch. At the top the alpine roads are worth riding on.
sides.highlights: At Compatsch the view across the pasture to the Langkofel and Plattkofel.

sella-nevea.intro: A quiet saddle between the Kanin and the Montasch, framed by high limestone walls. The road leaves the Predil route at the Raibler See and practically ends in the ski resort; there is hardly any traffic.

sides.character: A long, gentle approach from Tarvisio via Cave del Predil, first past the lake, then up in steps with a few short steeper pitches between the rock walls.
sides.highlights: The Raibler See on the way, the walls of the Kanin and the Montasch at the top.

selvino.intro: Bergamo's home climb: out of the Val Seriana in a famous run of hairpins up to the Selvino plateau. This is where the area learns to climb, and the continuation via Aviatico into the Val Serina makes a loop of it.

sides.character: From Nembro up the valley side in closely stacked hairpins, with changing ramps and the odd flatter stretch. The Val Seriana below you.
sides.highlights: The view back down the hairpins and the Val Seriana.

semnoz.intro: Annecy's home mountain, straight from the lakeshore up to the Crêt de Châtillon. In 2013 the Tour's penultimate stage finished here, won by Nairo Quintana. At the top the panorama reaches from the Bauges to Mont Blanc.

sides.character: From Annecy long and steady through forest, with no real break and no nasty surprises. Only above the tree line does the summit ridge open out.
sides.highlights: On the Crêt de Châtillon the panorama as far as Mont Blanc.

sestriere.intro: A regular of the Giro and the Tour. In 1952 Fausto Coppi won here at one of the Tour's first summit finishes, and in 1992 Claudio Chiappucci arrived alone after a long breakaway. Plain as scenery, heavy with history.

sides.character: Even from Cesana on a wide road with few hairpins, without surprises. A climb that is easy to pace.

sighignola.intro: The Balcone d'Italia: the road ends at the Swiss border on a ledge a good 1,000 m above Lake Lugano. Lugano below, and on a clear day the four-thousanders of the Valais on the horizon.

sides.character: From Lanzo d'Intelvi short and quiet up a few hairpins, steepest at the bottom and easing towards the top.
sides.highlights: The viewing ledge above Lugano at the end of the road.

silvretta-hochalpenstrasse.intro: The toll road between the Montafon and the Paznaun reaches the Bielerhöhe and the Silvretta reservoir at the top. On the Vorarlberg side a dense run of hairpins climbs to the Vermunt reservoir.

sides.character: From Partenen steeply up many hairpins to the Vermunt reservoir, then flatter along the water, with a dip, to the Bielerhöhe. The hairpins make the climb.
sides.highlights: The Vermunt and Silvretta reservoirs.

sides.character: From Galtür gentle and stepped up an open high valley, with few hairpins. A wide, calm descent.

simplonpass.intro: Napoleon had the Simplon road between Brig and Domodossola built; at the top stand the hospice and a stone eagle. Wide and busy, but even.

sides.character: Even from Brig on a wide road with few hairpins, across the Ganter bridge and through galleries.
sides.highlights: The Ganter bridge.

sides.character: From Gondo at the border through the narrow Gondo gorge with galleries, then more open past Simplon Dorf.
sides.highlights: The Gondo gorge.

soelkpass.intro: One of the few road crossings of the Niedere Tauern, through the Sölk valleys nature park from the Enns valley to the Mur valley. Little traffic, a lot of forest and a bare summit.

sides.character: From Stein an der Enns long through the Großsölk valley, stepped with flat stretches, steeper only higher up. As a descent long and quiet.
From Schöder shorter and steeper, the gradient increasing towards the top, with a few hairpins. The better way up.

sommet-bucher.intro: A lookout summit in the middle of the Queyras, reached by a narrow paved forest road. At the top an all-round view opens over the valleys and mountains of the Queyras.

sides.character: From Ville-Vieille steadily steep through larch forest, hairpin after hairpin on a narrow road. No resting point up to the summit, but a reliable rhythm.
sides.highlights: From the summit, the all-round view over the Guil and Aigue Agnelle valleys.

soriska-planina.intro: The quiet pass south of Bohinj, with a view of the Julian Alps.

sides.character: From Bohinjska Bistrica in steady hairpins through forest to the pasture.
sides.highlights: The view across the Bohinj basin to Triglav.

sides.character: From Železniki long through the Selška valley, then via Sorica to the top.
sides.highlights: The village of Sorica.

spitzingsattel.intro: The after-work climb of Munich's cyclists: a short steep ramp with a mountain lake behind it.

sides.character: From Schliersee flat to Neuhaus, then a good two kilometres steep in hairpins up to the saddle.
sides.highlights: The Spitzingsee behind the saddle.

spluegenpass.intro: The Splügen links the Rheinwald with Chiavenna. On the Swiss side the hairpins stack tightly one above the other; the Italian side climbs long from the valley, through galleries and past the Montespluga reservoir.

sides.character: Short and even from Splügen: a dense stairway of hairpins above the village, easy to read in either direction.
sides.highlights: The village of Splügen with its stone houses.

sides.character: Very long from Chiavenna, stepped with countless hairpins, some of them in galleries. Because of the tunnels and tight bends, better uphill.
sides.highlights: The Montespluga reservoir just before the border.

sportgastein.intro: The Gasteiner Alpenstraße leads from Bad Gastein into the furthest corner of the Gastein valley, the Nassfeld beneath the three-thousanders of the Goldberg group. A dead end with no through traffic and traces of the old gold mining.

sides.character: From Bad Gastein via Böckstein into the narrowing valley, in steps with short steep ramps and flatter stretches between them, almost without hairpins.
sides.highlights: The wide valley head of the Nassfeld beneath the peaks.

staffal.intro: The Walser valley on the south side of the Monte Rosa, with German place names and wooden houses. A climb of almost 40 kilometres in which the glaciers only come into view at the very top.

sides.character: From the Roman bridge in Pont-Saint-Martin long and flat, then up the valley in steps, with a few steeper hairpins before Gressoney-Saint-Jean and at the end.
sides.highlights: The lake of Gressoney-Saint-Jean with the Lyskamm behind it.

staller-sattel.intro: High above the Antholzer See the road leads from the Pustertal into the Defereggental, one of the quietest over 2,000 m. The southern ramp is single-track and opened to one direction at a time, which spares it most of the cars.

sides.character: From Antholz Mittertal past the lake, then single-track up the wall in hairpins, steeper towards the top. Uphill, with the lake below, the finer direction.
sides.highlights: The Antholzer See below the hairpins.

sides.character: From the Defereggental at Erlsbach first with a steep ramp, then more evenly across pastures to the top. Wider than the south side and more open as a descent.
sides.highlights: At the saddle, the small Obersee.

stoderzinken.intro: One of the most beautiful viewpoint roads in Styria, onto a limestone massif opposite the Dachstein. Short, steep and hardly used.

sides.character: From Gröbming steeply through forest and in hairpins up to the pastures, narrow and without a flat section.
sides.highlights: The little Friedenskircherl chapel on the rock and the view of the Dachstein and the Tauern.

strada-della-forra.intro: The road out of the Brasa gorge from Lake Garda up to Tremosine, hewn into overhanging rock and through dark tunnels. Known too from the car chase at the start of the James Bond film "Quantum of Solace".

sides.character: From the lakeshore into the narrow gorge, beneath rock overhangs and through tunnels, then up in steps onto the plateau. The gradient is secondary; the narrowness and the traffic are not.
sides.highlights: The rock overhangs of the gorge; at the top the view from Tremosine over Lake Garda.

stubaital.intro: A valley head below the Stubai glacier, half an hour from Innsbruck. More an outing than a climb, with a steeper finish.

sides.character: From Schönberg long and flat through the villages, steeper beyond Ranalt in a few hairpins up to the Mutterbergalm.
sides.highlights: The Grawa waterfall shortly before the head of the valley.

sudelfeld.intro: From the Leitzach valley across the ski slopes of the Sudelfeld over into the Inn valley. The short west side from Bayrischzell is steep; the long east side passes the Tatzelwurm waterfall.

sides.character: From Bayrischzell short and steep, getting steeper towards the top, almost without hairpins. Quickly done uphill, straight and fast downhill.
From Oberaudorf long and in steps through forest past the Tatzelwurm, with flatter sections in between. As the descent into the Inn valley, the calmer, longer choice.
sides.highlights: The Tatzelwurm waterfall along the way.

sulden.intro: A detour into the Sulden valley to the mountaineering village below the Ortler and the Königspitze. A fine addition to the Stelvio.

sides.character: From Gomagoi up the narrow valley, with a changing gradient and some hairpins; near the top the view opens onto the glaciers.
sides.highlights: The Ortler and the Königspitze at the head of the valley.

superbagneres.intro: The balcony above Luchon, with the highest peaks of the Pyrenees opposite.

sides.character: From Luchon on the Saint-Aventin road, then steadily in hairpins to the resort.
sides.highlights: The Grand Hôtel and the view of the Maladeta.

sustenpass.intro: Opened in 1946 and planned from the start for motor traffic. An even gradient, wide bends and the Steingletscher below the summit tunnel.

sides.character: From Innertkirchen very long up the Gadmental, in steps, then in hairpins past the Steingletscher near the top. The glacier comes into view as you climb.
sides.highlights: The Steingletscher and the Steinsee below the top.

sides.character: From Wassen even up the Meiental, hardly any hairpins, with tunnels and galleries. A flowing, readable descent.

thyon-2000.intro: One of the longest climbs in the Valais, straight out of Sion to over 2,000 m.

sides.character: Out of Sion in hairpins to Vex, then steadily steep via Les Collons up to the station.
sides.highlights: The view across the Rhône valley.

timmelsjoch.intro: The high road between the Ötztal and the Passeier valley is the last and hardest climb of the Ötztaler Radmarathon. On the South Tyrol side a long, wild road with tunnels.

sides.character: From Sölden via Hochgurgl, stepped with a dip and flatter sections. Wide and well built, the more pleasant side to descend.
From St. Leonhard very long up the Passeier valley, stepped, then in hairpins and through tunnels below rock walls near the top. The Ötztaler side, the one to climb.
sides.highlights: The hairpins below the rock walls just before the top.

tre-cime-di-lavaredo.intro: The toll road ends at the Rifugio Auronzo below the south faces of the Tre Cime. The Giro has finished here several times; in 2013 Vincenzo Nibali won in a snowstorm.

sides.character: Gentle at first from Lake Misurina, with a short drop after the toll booth, then the steep final kilometres in a few hairpins up to the car park at the hut.
sides.highlights: Start at Lake Misurina, the Tre Cime right above you at the top.

triebener-tauern.intro: A quiet crossing of the Niedere Tauern between the Enns and Mur valleys.

sides.character: From Trieben steeply through the narrow valley of the Triebenbach and in hairpins to Hohentauern.
sides.highlights: The high valley of Hohentauern.

sides.character: From St. Johann gently through the upper Pöls valley.
sides.highlights: The quiet meadows of the Pöls valley.

turracher-hoehe.intro: The crossing between Carinthia and Styria, with ramps of over 20 %, is considered one of Austria's steepest passes. At the top lies the Turracher See between ski lifts and Swiss stone pine forest.

sides.character: From Ebene Reichenau the classic side: alternating very steep ramps and flatter stretches, with hairpins. The steep bits are better ridden up.
From Predlitz through the Turrach valley, stepped with flat stretches between steeper sections and only a few hairpins.

ultental-weissbrunn.intro: A dead-end valley behind Lana, past reservoirs to the Weißbrunnsee beneath the Weißbrunnspitze. Little gradient, little traffic, old farmsteads and, at St. Gertraud, the ancient Ultental larches: the counterpart to the Dolomite passes.

sides.character: Up the valley from St. Walburg along the Zoggler reservoir, flat with a few steep steps, the last one before the Weißbrunnsee. Quiet, a ride without hurry.
sides.highlights: The ancient larches near St. Gertraud.

umbrailpass.intro: Switzerland's highest road pass, on the border just below the Stelvio. Part of it was still gravel until 2015; today it is paved throughout.

sides.character: From Santa Maria steadily steep in many hairpins through forest and then over open slopes. Quieter than the Stelvio, but hardly easier.
sides.highlights: At the top the road joins the Bormio side of the Stelvio.

val-bavona.intro: The uppermost Maggia valley: a narrow road between granite walls, rockfalls and waterfalls, through hamlets without mains electricity to San Carlo. Hardly any cars, a lot of stone and a valley unlike any other in Ticino.

sides.character: Up the valley from Cevio: gently in steps along the river, a few short steeper bits, almost flat in between. The rock walls close in ever further.
sides.highlights: The waterfall at Foroglio, with a grotto there for a break.

val-di-genova.intro: The waterfall valley on the edge of the Adamello, from the Val Rendena up beneath the glaciers at the Malga Bedole. Right at the entrance the Nardis falls tumble down; higher up the road is closed to cars by day in summer.

sides.character: Up the valley from Carisolo in steps, flat stretches alternating with short steep rises beside the stream. The further in, the narrower the road and the closer the glaciers.
sides.highlights: The Nardis falls at the entrance to the valley.

val-thorens.intro: The ascent to the highest ski resort in the Alps runs up the whole Belleville valley. In 2019 the last mountain stage of the Tour finished here, won by Vincenzo Nibali.

sides.character: From Moûtiers long and stepped via Saint-Martin-de-Belleville and Les Menuires, never steep, never flat, with many hairpins. Ski lifts rather than summit views at the top.

valgrisenche.intro: A dead end in the Aosta valley that leads past the Beauregard reservoir up to beneath the glaciers of the Grande Sassière. After the lake almost nothing follows, just quiet and rock.

sides.character: Up from Arvier in steps, steep ramps and calmer sections in turn, in the upper part along the flank high above the reservoir.
sides.highlights: The Beauregard reservoir with the glaciers above.

valle-maira.intro: The quietest of the Piedmontese valleys, away from mass tourism. At its end the rock tooth of the Rocca Provenzale rises above Chiappera; you ride here for the peace, not the gradient.

sides.character: Up the valley from Acceglio, even and moderately steep, with a few hairpins through larches and pastures to the valley head.
sides.highlights: The Rocca Provenzale above Chiappera.

valle-verzasca.intro: Beyond Gordola over the Contra dam, from which James Bond jumped in GoldenEye, then along the clear green water of the Verzasca to Sonogno. One of the finest valleys in Ticino, full of bathers in high summer.

sides.character: Up the valley from Gordola: first in hairpins to the dam and along the reservoir, then in steps beside the river, between stone villages and granite to the head of the valley.
sides.highlights: The double-arched stone bridge Ponte dei Salti at Lavertezzo.

vallee-de-l-ubaye.intro: The upper Ubaye valley is one of the quietest roads in the Western Alps and ends at Maljasset beneath the three-thousanders. A valley for an easy ride, far from pass traffic.

sides.character: From Saint-Paul-sur-Ubaye up the valley a rolling up and down with short ramps and descents, hardly any net gradient. The valley grows ever narrower and more ringed by high peaks.

vallee-de-la-claree.intro: One of the loveliest valleys in the Western Alps: larches, old hamlets and a stream, with the upper part closed to cars on summer days. Little gradient, plenty of scenery, right next to Briançon.

sides.character: From Val-des-Prés up the valley via Névache to Laval, gentle and in steps, a little steeper at the top. The further you go, the quieter and wilder the valley becomes.
sides.highlights: The hamlets of Névache and the quiet head of the valley at Laval.

vallee-des-chapieux.intro: From Bourg-Saint-Maurice via Les Chapieux into the Vallée des Glaciers, until the road stops at the foot of the Mont Blanc massif. A world's end of pastures and glaciers, away from the Roselend traffic.

sides.character: From Bourg-Saint-Maurice through forest in hairpins at first, then along the valley, sometimes flatter, sometimes steeper, to Les Chapieux and on along a narrow road to the valley head.
sides.highlights: The end of the road in front of the glaciers of the Mont Blanc massif.

valmeinier-1800.intro: A dead end up to the ski station of Valmeinier 1800, meant for anyone staying in Valloire who wants a quiet extra to the Télégraphe and the Galibier. Little known and correspondingly quiet in summer.

sides.character: From the junction in the Valloire basin steadily up through a few hairpins, a little steeper towards the end. A short climb that fits well onto an easy day.

valsavarenche.intro: The middle one of the valleys of the Gran Paradiso, entirely within the national park. The road ends at Pont beneath the summit, where the paths to the huts begin; with luck you will see ibex on the way.

sides.character: Up the valley from Villeneuve: first in hairpins out of the Aosta valley, then long and even through forest and meadows to the head of the valley.
sides.highlights: At the valley head in Pont, the Gran Paradiso in view.

valvestino.intro: From Lake Garda at Gargnano into the mountains behind it: first up in hairpins, then through tunnels and galleries high above the fjord-like Valvestino reservoir to Magasa. Almost car-free and one of the finest roads on the western shore.

sides.character: Inland from Gargnano: steeply up in hairpins above the lake, then in steps with counter-climbs along the reservoir, and finally up to the mountain village of Magasa.
sides.highlights: The view down onto the green reservoir.

verbier.intro: The ski resort above the Val de Bagnes where the 2009 Tour de France finished. Not a long climb, but one without a breather.

sides.character: From Le Châble steadily steep in many hairpins over meadows and through chalet settlements up to the village square.
sides.highlights: The view across the Val de Bagnes to the Grand Combin.

villacher-alpenstrasse.intro: The toll road climbs from Villach onto the Dobratsch, the Villacher Alpe, in its nature park. Wide views at the top over the Carinthian lakes, the Karawanks and the Julian Alps.

sides.character: From the edge of town at a steady 6 to 7 % through forest, with a few hairpins and viewpoints, up to the Rosstratten car park.
sides.highlights: View from the Rosstratten onto the Julian Alps and the Karawanks

villard-reymond.intro: A detour for anyone who finds the Ornon too tame: the narrow road winds up in hairpins to a small mountain village high above the Oisans. Hardly any traffic, but plenty of gradient.

sides.character: From the junction on the Ornon road narrow and irregularly steep, hairpin after hairpin up the slope. The gradient changes all the time, and a rhythm is hard to find.
sides.highlights: At the top the view down into the Oisans.

villnoesstal.intro: The valley beneath the Geisler peaks, Reinhold Messner's home and the subject of countless photos of the church of St. Johann in Ranui against the wall. Quiet, because it leads nowhere, with the Zanser Alm as the goal.

sides.character: From Klausen steep at first out of the Eisack valley, then in steps up the valley, noticeably steeper again from St. Magdalena to the Zanser Alm. The Geisler stay in front of your wheel the whole way.
sides.highlights: The church of St. Johann in Ranui in front of the Geisler peaks.

vorderkaser-pfossental.intro: A side valley of the Schnalstal, reached by a narrow, steep road up to the Vorderkaser inn. Barely known and barely used, but one of the steepest ramps around.

sides.character: From the junction in the Schnalstal steep and steeper still towards the top, with few hairpins and hardly any respite. Short, but only comfortable with a small gear.
sides.highlights: At the top, the Vorderkaser inn for a stop.

vrsic.intro: Slovenia's highest pass crosses the Julian Alps from Kranjska Gora to the Soča valley, with 50 numbered hairpins, cobbled on the north side. It was built in the First World War by Russian prisoners of war, remembered by the Russian Chapel.

sides.character: From Kranjska Gora past Lake Jasna, then through forest in cobbled hairpins, steeper towards the top. The cobbles speak against descending here.
sides.highlights: The Russian Chapel on the way, and Prisojnik and Mojstrovka at the top

sides.character: From the Trenta valley along the Soča and then in many hairpins up the southern flank, steeper towards the top. As a descent with views into the Soča valley.
sides.highlights: The emerald water of the Soča in the valley

vue-des-alpes.intro: The name says it all: the Alpine view of the Neuchâtel Jura.

sides.character: From Valangin through the Val de Ruz and steadily to the top.
sides.highlights: The Alpine view at the top.

sides.character: From La Chaux-de-Fonds short and gentle.
sides.highlights: The pastures of the Jura heights.

wallbergstrasse.intro: A car-free mountain road above the Tegernsee, the training climb of the Bavarian Oberland.

sides.character: From Rottach-Egern to the valley station, then in many hairpins steadily steep through forest up to the Wallberghaus.
sides.highlights: The view over the Tegernsee into the foothills.

weinebene.intro: The highest road pass of the Koralpe, with long climbs out of the wine country and out of the Lavant valley.

sides.character: From Deutschlandsberg through the gorge and long and steady through forest up to the alpine heights.
sides.highlights: The view across the Styrian hill country.

sides.character: From Wolfsberg in the Lavant valley steadily via Prössing.
sides.highlights: The view across the Lavant valley to the Saualpe.

weissenstein.intro: One of the steepest passes in Switzerland, short and hard.

sides.character: From Oberdorf in tight hairpins steep all the way through forest.
sides.highlights: The view across the Swiss plateau to the Alps.

sides.character: From Gänsbrunnen shorter and a little gentler through forest.
sides.highlights: The pastures of the Jura ridge.

wildhaus.intro: The link from Liechtenstein into the Toggenburg, with the Churfirsten above the top.

sides.character: From Gams in the Rhine valley steeply in hairpins up the slope.
sides.highlights: The view across the Rhine valley to Liechtenstein.

sides.character: From Nesslau gently through the upper Toggenburg via Unterwasser.
sides.highlights: The Churfirsten above Unterwasser.

windische-hoehe.intro: A small pass that links the Gail and Drau valleys for a loop from Villach.

sides.character: From Feistritz steadily through forest.
sides.highlights: The view across the Gail valley to the Carnic Alps.

sides.character: From Paternion via Kreuzen along the slope, moderate.
sides.highlights: The view into the Drau valley.

wolfgangpass.intro: The crossing from the Prättigau to Davos, the way to the Flüela.

sides.character: From Klosters steadily through forest up to the saddle above the Davosersee.
sides.highlights: The Davosersee beyond the top.

wurzenpass.intro: A border crossing into Slovenia whose reputation comes from the gradient, not the scenery. The northern ramp is short and brutally steep in its final kilometres, and lorries use it too.

sides.character: From Riegersdorf straight into long, straight steep sections, hardly any hairpins to catch your breath. A trial of strength uphill, unpleasant downhill because of the gradient and the traffic.
From Kranjska Gora moderately through forest, steeper only towards the border. The easy side, and the better choice as the descent into Slovenia.

zillertaler-hoehenstrasse.intro: One of Austria's hardest roads: from the floor of the Zillertal up onto an alpine ridge with a view of the glaciers.

sides.character: Steep right from Ried through the hillside hamlets, then long ramps above 10 % through forest and over pastures up to the Melchboden.
sides.highlights: The view from the Melchboden across the Zillertal to the main Zillertal ridge.

zinal.intro: The second dead end of the Val d'Anniviers next to Moiry, gentler, with the Imperial Crown at the head of the valley.

sides.character: At the bottom the valley road into the Val d'Anniviers, from Vissoie steadily via Ayer to Zinal.
sides.highlights: The ring of summits at the head of the valley.
